nangchen.t: A kingdom of nomad and farming clans in the upper Mekong and Yangtze valleys of Kham, famous for its many Kagyu monasteries.
nangchen.o: Nangchen, in today's [[e:yushu-tibetan-autonomous-prefecture|Yushu]] region of southern Qinghai, emerged as a principality under a hereditary royal family in the Mongol period. Tradition credits its kings with receiving recognition from the [[s:sakya-regime|Sakya]] lama [[e:drogon-chogyal-phagpa|Phagpa]] in the 13th century, and their house ruled a federation of local tribes from the royal seat at Nangchen.
nangchen.r: The king presided over some twenty-five tribes, mostly yak-herding nomads with some farming villages, each under its own chief. The kingdom was a stronghold of the [[e:drukpa-kagyu|Drukpa]], [[e:barom-kagyu|Barom]] and [[e:drigung-kagyu|Drigung Kagyu]] traditions, with dozens of monasteries. From the 18th century it was nominally under [[e:qing-empire|Qing]] supervision from [[e:xining|Xining]], while maintaining close religious ties with [[e:lhasa|Lhasa]].
nangchen.e: In the Sino-Tibetan fighting of 1932 the Muslim warlords of Qinghai took effective control, and Nangchen's autonomy ended. The royal family kept some local standing until the 1950s, when the [[s:peoples-republic-of-china|People's Republic of China]] abolished the old order.

ndzundza-ndebele-kingdom.t: A Southern Ndebele kingdom of the eastern Transvaal that held out against the Boers from its cave fortress until 1883.
ndzundza-ndebele-kingdom.o: [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele]] tradition says the Ndzundza branch split from the senior Manala house after a dispute among the sons of the ruler Musi in the 17th century. The Ndzundza settled east of present-day [[e:pretoria|Pretoria]] and later established a stronghold at KwaMaza near modern [[e:roossenekal|Roossenekal]].
ndzundza-ndebele-kingdom.r: The king ruled through royal kin and regimental age-sets, and the kingdom recovered from defeat by [[e:mzilikazi|Mzilikazi]] in the 1820s under [[e:mabhoko|Mabhoko]] (Mapoch), who used the caves of KwaMaza as a defensive refuge. Ndzundza homesteads were later noted for their striking painted walls and women's beadwork, which became emblems of [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele]] identity.
ndzundza-ndebele-kingdom.e: In 1882 King [[e:nyabela|Nyabela]] sheltered the Pedi rebel [[e:mampuru-ii|Mampuru]], and the [[s:south-african-republic|South African Republic]] besieged KwaMaza. After a long siege the Ndzundza surrendered in 1883; their land was confiscated and the people indentured to [[e:boers|Boer]] farmers.

nagar.t: Nagar, a major city of the northern Syrian plains at Tell Brak, famed in the 3rd millennium BCE for breeding prized draught equids and later seized by Akkad.
nagar.o: Tell [[e:brak|Brak]] in the [[e:khabur-river|Khabur]] basin had been one of the largest settlements of northern [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]] since the 4th millennium BCE. By c. 2600 BCE it was the centre of a kingdom called Nagar, which appears in the [[s:ebla|Ebla]] archives as a regional power on the route between [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and the [[e:tigris|Tigris]].
nagar.r: [[s:ebla|Ebla]] texts show Nagar exchanging gifts, envoys and royal marriages with its western neighbour, and supplying expensive kunga, hybrid draught animals bred from donkeys and wild asses, used to pull royal vehicles. Little is known of its internal government, since few texts have been found at the site itself.
nagar.e: Around 2300 BCE the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]] took control; [[e:naram-sin|Naram-Sin]] built a massive fortified storehouse at Tell [[e:brak|Brak]]. After [[e:akkad|Akkad's]] collapse a Hurrian kingdom called Nawar ruled from the city, and Tell Brak stayed occupied into the 2nd millennium BCE.

niya.t: Niya, a small kingdom of the middle Orontes, known for the elephant herds that pharaoh Thutmose III hunted in its marshes.
niya.o: Niya lay in the middle [[e:orontes-river|Orontes]] valley, probably near [[e:apamea-syria|Apamea]], in a region of marshes and fertile land. It emerged in the 15th century BCE as a minor kingdom in the orbit of the [[s:mitanni-empire|Mitanni Empire]].
niya.r: Little is known of its government. [[e:thutmose-iii|Thutmose III]] of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] recorded hunting about 120 elephants there, and the city appears in the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]] and the archives of [[s:kingdom-of-mukish|Alalakh]]. According to Hittite sources, its king Takuwa sought peace with [[e:suppiluliuma-i|Suppiluliuma I]], but his brother Aki-[[e:teshub|Teshub]] turned the city against the [[e:hittite-empire|Hittites]].
niya.e: [[e:suppiluliuma-i|Suppiluliuma I]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] took Niya c. 1340 BCE during his conquest of [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], and it disappears as a kingdom.

nilgiri-state.t: A small princely state in the hills of Balasore in Odisha, the first of the Orissa states to be taken over by the provincial government after independence.
nilgiri-state.o: The ruling family claimed descent from the [[e:bhanja-dynasty|Bhanja]] rulers of the region, and tradition dates the state to the early 16th century. Its capital was Rajnilgiri, below the Nilgiri hills inland from [[e:balasore|Balasore]].
nilgiri-state.r: Nilgiri was a small state of farmland and wooded hills, known for its stone carving. It was one of the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]] under British supervision after 1803. In 1946–1947 the [[e:praja-mandal|Praja Mandal]] led protests against the Raja, and Adivasi unrest followed.
nilgiri-state.e: In November 1947 the government of [[e:odisha|Orissa]] took over Nilgiri's administration, the first such takeover among the Orissa states, and the merger was formalised in 1948. It is now in [[e:balasore|Balasore]] district.

northern-liao.t: A rump Liao regime proclaimed at Yanjing (Beijing) in 1122 while the last Khitan emperor was in flight, which repelled the Song but fell to the Jurchen within the year.
northern-liao.o: In 1122, as the [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] of the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234) overran the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]] and Emperor [[e:emperor-tianzuo-of-liao|Tianzuo]] fled into the western steppe, Khitan and Chinese officials at [[e:beijing|Yanjing]] enthroned [[e:yelu-chun|Yelü Chun]], an imperial kinsman, as emperor, in effect deposing Tianzuo.
northern-liao.r: The regime held the [[e:beijing|Yanjing]] region and the passes to the north. [[e:yelu-chun|Yelü Chun]] died within months, and his widow [[e:xiao-defei|Xiao Defei]] governed as empress dowager. With commanders such as [[e:yelu-dashi|Yelü Dashi]], its army defeated two [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]] attempts to take Yanjing in 1122, revealing [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] weakness to the [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]].
northern-liao.e: At the end of 1122 the [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] ruler [[e:emperor-taizu-of-jin|Aguda]] took [[e:beijing|Yanjing]] with little resistance; [[e:xiao-defei|Xiao Defei]] fled and was later killed by [[e:emperor-tianzuo-of-liao|Tianzuo]]. Some followers set up a short-lived Xi kingdom in 1123. [[e:yelu-dashi|Yelü Dashi]] went on to found the [[s:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]].

nurmekund.t: Small Estonian district in the centre of the country, mentioned in Henry of Livonia's chronicle and conquered in the 1220s.
nurmekund.o: Nurmekund, called Normegunde in the sources, was a minor Estonian land in central [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]], between [[s:sakala|Sakala]], [[s:jarvamaa|Järvamaa]] and [[s:alempois|Alempois]]. It is known only from brief mentions in the chronicle of the Livonian [[e:crusade|crusade]].
nurmekund.r: It was probably a union of a few parishes under elders, sharing the customs and pagan religion of the larger Estonian counties around it. No leaders or details of its organisation are recorded.
nurmekund.e: Nurmekund was subdued during the conquest of [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]], completed in 1224, and passed to the [[s:livonian-brothers-of-the-sword|Livonian Brothers of the Sword]] and later the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]].

nizari-ismaili-state.t: The network of mountain castles in Iran and Syria ruled by the Nizari Ismailis, famous in legend as the 'Assassins', that defied the Seljuks for over 150 years.
nizari-ismaili-state.o: [[e:hasan-i-sabbah|Hasan-i Sabbah]], an [[e:ismailism|Ismaili]] missionary, seized the castle of [[e:alamut|Alamut]] in the [[e:alborz|Alborz]] in 1090. When the [[s:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimid Caliphate]] passed over the heir [[e:nizar-ibn-al-mustansir|Nizar]] in 1094, Hasan and his followers supported [[e:nizari-ismailism|Nizar's]] line, breaking with [[e:cairo|Cairo]] and founding an independent Nizari movement in [[e:iran|Iran]].
nizari-ismaili-state.r: The state was a scattered collection of fortresses in [[e:rudbar-of-alamut|Rudbar]], [[e:quhistan|Quhistan]] and, from the 12th century, [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], where [[e:rashid-al-din-sinan|Rashid al-Din Sinan]] became known to the crusaders as the 'Old Man of the Mountain'. Unable to match Seljuk armies, the [[e:nizari-ismailism|Nizaris]] used targeted killings by devotees (fida'is) against hostile leaders. [[e:alamut|Alamut]] had a famous library; the scholar Nasir al-Din al-Tusi lived among them. In 1164 [[e:hasan-ii-of-alamut|Hasan II]] proclaimed the qiyama, the spiritual resurrection.
nizari-ismaili-state.e: [[e:hulagu-khan|Hulagu's]] Mongol army forced the last [[e:imam|imam]], [[e:rukn-al-din-khurshah|Rukn al-Din Khurshah]], to surrender [[e:alamut|Alamut]] in 1256; he was later killed. The Syrian castles fell to the [[s:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluk Sultanate]] by 1273. The [[e:aga-khan|Aga Khans]] trace their [[e:imamate|imamate]] to this line.

new-zealand.t: The fully independent island nation that emerged from the Dominion of New Zealand in 1947, known for its Treaty of Waitangi settlements and nuclear-free policy.
new-zealand.o: New Zealand gained full legislative independence when Parliament adopted the [[e:statute-of-westminster-1931|Statute of Westminster]] in November 1947, under Prime Minister [[e:peter-fraser|Peter Fraser]], ending the [[s:dominion-of-new-zealand|Dominion of New Zealand]]. The appointed upper house, the Legislative Council, was abolished in 1951, leaving a single-chamber parliament, and separate New Zealand citizenship had been created in 1948.
new-zealand.r: The [[e:anzus|ANZUS Treaty]] of 1951 tied New Zealand to the [[s:united-states|United States]] and [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Australia]]. [[e:britain|Britain's]] entry into the [[e:european-economic-community|European Economic Community]] in 1973 forced a search for new markets. The [[e:waitangi-tribunal|Waitangi Tribunal]], created in 1975, investigated breaches of the [[e:treaty-of-waitangi|Treaty of Waitangi]] and led to large settlements with iwi. From 1984 Labour's market reforms reshaped the economy, and nuclear-free legislation broke the ANZUS alliance; French agents bombed the [[e:sinking-of-the-rainbow-warrior|Rainbow Warrior]] in [[e:auckland|Auckland]] in 1985.
new-zealand.e: Proportional representation was introduced in 1996. Te reo Māori became an official language in 1987. New Zealand remains a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] with the British monarch as head of state, known internationally for leaders such as [[e:jacinda-ardern|Jacinda Ardern]].

nueva-vizcaya.t: The vast northern Spanish province of New Spain, covering today's Durango and Chihuahua, built on silver mining and frontier warfare.
nueva-vizcaya.o: [[e:francisco-de-ibarra|Francisco de Ibarra]], a Basque explorer funded by his uncle, a [[e:zacatecas|Zacatecas]] mining [[e:magnates|magnate]], led expeditions north from 1554 and became governor of the new province in 1562. He founded [[e:durango-city|Durango]] in 1563 as its capital and named the province after his home region, [[e:biscay|Biscay]].
nueva-vizcaya.r: The province's wealth came from [[e:silver|silver]] mines at Santa Bárbara, [[e:hidalgo-del-parral|Parral]], from 1631, and [[e:chihuahua-city|Chihuahua]]. Missions of the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] and [[e:franciscans|Franciscans]] pushed into the [[e:sierra-madre-occidental|Sierra Madre]], provoking the [[e:tepehuan-revolt|Tepehuán revolt]] of 1616 and [[e:raramuri|Tarahumara]] uprisings. Presidios guarded routes against [[e:apache|Apache]] and other raiders, and the [[e:camino-real-de-tierra-adentro|Camino Real]] linked it to [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]] and [[s:santa-fe-de-nuevo-mexico|Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico]].
nueva-vizcaya.e: From 1776 Nueva [[e:biscay|Vizcaya]] belonged to the [[s:commandancy-general-of-the-internal-provinces|Provincias Internas]], and in 1786 it became an intendancy. After independence it was divided in 1824 into the Mexican states of [[e:durango-city|Durango]] and [[e:chihuahua-city|Chihuahua]].

neo-inca-state.t: The last independent Inca state, which held out in the forested mountains of Vilcabamba for 35 years after the Spanish conquest of Cusco.
neo-inca-state.o: In 1536 the [[e:inca-empire|Inca]] ruler [[e:manco-inca|Manco Inca]], installed by the Spanish as a puppet, rebelled and besieged [[e:cusco|Cusco]] for months. After failing to retake the city, he withdrew in 1537 to [[e:vitcos|Vitcos]] and then Vilcabamba, a remote region in the montane forest northwest of Cusco, where he founded a new Inca state.
neo-inca-state.r: From Vilcabamba, [[e:manco-inca|Manco Inca]] waged [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] war against the Spanish and kept up [[e:inca-empire|Inca]] rituals and court life. After his murder in 1544 by Spanish refugees, his sons ruled in turn. [[e:sayri-tupac|Sayri Túpac]] accepted Spanish terms and left in 1558. [[e:titu-cusi-yupanqui|Titu Cusi Yupanqui]] negotiated with the Spanish, allowed missionaries and dictated an account of the conquest, the Instrucción, in 1570.
neo-inca-state.e: [[e:viceroy-of-india|Viceroy]] [[e:francisco-alvarez-de-toledo|Francisco de Toledo]] sent an expedition in 1572 that captured the last ruler, [[e:tupac-amaru|Túpac Amaru]], who was executed in [[e:cusco|Cusco]]. Vilcabamba was abandoned and forgotten until explorers, including [[e:hiram-bingham-iii|Hiram Bingham]] in 1911, rediscovered its ruins at [[e:espiritu-pampa|Espíritu Pampa]].

nuhashshe.t: Nuhashshe, a group of small Syrian kingdoms between the Orontes and the Euphrates, fought over by Mitanni, Egypt and the Hittites.
nuhashshe.o: The lands of Nuhashshe lay in the steppe and farmland south of [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]]. In the 15th century BCE their rulers were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:mitanni-empire|Mitanni Empire]], and the region appears in Egyptian records of campaigns by [[e:thutmose-iii|Thutmose III]] and in the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]].
nuhashshe.r: Nuhashshe was a cluster of local kingdoms rather than a single state, with a leading king who represented the region in treaties. Its rulers moved between Egyptian, Mitannian and Hittite loyalties as each power advanced.
nuhashshe.e: [[e:suppiluliuma-i|Suppiluliuma I]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] conquered the region in the 14th century BCE and made its king a [[e:vassal|vassal]] by treaty. Rebellions under [[e:mursili-ii|Mursili II]] were suppressed, and the region later reappeared as [[s:luash|Lu'ash]].

neapolis.t: Greek 'new city' on the Bay of Naples, founded from Cumae, which kept its Greek speech and customs long after becoming Rome's ally in 326 BCE.
neapolis.o: [[s:cumae|Cumae]] founded Neapolis around 470 BCE beside an older settlement, [[e:parthenope-city|Parthenope]], named after a Siren whose tomb was shown there and which became known as Palaepolis, 'old city'. The new town was laid out on a regular grid whose main streets still shape central [[e:naples|Naples]].
neapolis.r: Neapolis grew through trade and gained importance after [[s:cumae|Cumae]] fell to the Campanians around 421 BCE. Athenian settlers are said to have joined it in the 5th century BCE, and it later admitted Campanian families to citizenship. Its coins with a man-headed bull and its torch race in honour of [[e:parthenope-city|Parthenope]] are well known. It remained a centre of Greek culture in [[e:campania|Campania]].
neapolis.e: After a Roman siege in 327–326 BCE, the city made a treaty with [[e:rome|Rome]] on favourable terms and became a loyal naval ally. It kept [[e:greek-language|Greek language]] and institutions into the Empire, attracting Roman writers such as [[e:virgil|Virgil]], and grew into [[e:naples|Naples]].

northern-yan.t: The last of the north-eastern Yan states, ruled from Longcheng first by Gao Yun and then by the Chinese Feng family, until the Northern Wei conquest of 436.
northern-yan.o: In 407 the general [[e:feng-ba|Feng Ba]] and [[e:gao-yun|Gao Yun]], a man of [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] descent adopted into the [[s:later-yan|Later Yan]] royal family, killed the tyrannical emperor [[e:murong-xi|Murong Xi]] at [[e:chaoyang-liaoning|Longcheng]] (Chaoyang, [[e:liaoning|Liaoning]]). [[e:gao|Gao]] Yun became Heavenly King of a new Yan.
northern-yan.r: After [[e:gao-yun|Gao Yun]] was assassinated in 409, [[e:feng-ba|Feng Ba]] took the throne and ruled moderately, reducing taxes and encouraging farming. Northern Yan kept close ties with [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] and the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran Khaganate]]. Feng Ba's brother [[e:feng-hong|Feng Hong]] seized power in 430 amid family bloodshed, and the state was soon besieged by the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]].
northern-yan.e: In 436 [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] armies closed on [[e:chaoyang-liaoning|Longcheng]] and [[e:feng-hong|Feng Hong]] fled to [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] with his people; he was killed there in 438. His granddaughter became [[e:empress-dowager-feng|Empress Dowager Feng]], who later reformed the Northern Wei.

nabha-state.t: One of the three Phulkian Sikh states of Punjab, whose Maharaja Ripudaman Singh was deposed in 1923 for his nationalist sympathies.
nabha-state.o: [[e:hamir-singh-of-nabha|Hamir Singh]], a descendant of Phul and kinsman of the rulers of [[s:patiala-state|Patiala]], established his own state in the [[e:malwa|Malwa]] region of [[e:punjab|Punjab]] in the 1750s and 1760s and founded the town of Nabha. The family held the title of Raja.
nabha-state.r: Nabha accepted British protection with the other [[e:cis-sutlej-states|Cis-Sutlej states]] in 1809. Raja [[e:jaswant-singh-of-nabha|Jaswant Singh]]'s successor was deposed after the [[e:first-anglo-sikh-war|First Anglo-Sikh War]] for siding with [[e:lahore|Lahore]], but later rulers supported the British in 1857. [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:ripudaman-singh|Ripudaman Singh]] backed [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] reform and Indian nationalist causes and was forced to abdicate in 1923, prompting the [[e:jaito-morcha|Jaito morcha]] protest by the [[e:akali-movement|Akalis]].
nabha-state.e: Nabha acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947 and in 1948 joined the [[s:patiala-and-east-punjab-states-union|Patiala and East Punjab States Union]], which became part of [[e:punjab|Punjab]] in 1956.

nizari-ismailis-of-syria.t: The Syrian branch of the Nizari Ismailis, the 'Assassins' of Crusader legend, who ruled a network of mountain castles around Masyaf.
nizari-ismailis-of-syria.o: [[e:nizari-ismailism|Nizari]] missionaries sent from [[e:alamut|Alamut]] in [[e:iran|Iran]] first worked in [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] and [[e:damascus|Damascus]] but were driven out by massacres. From 1132 they acquired castles in the [[e:syrian-coastal-mountain-range|Jabal Bahra]], the coastal mountains of [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]], including [[e:qadmus|Qadmus]], [[e:al-kahf-castle|Kahf]] and in 1140-1141 [[e:masyaf|Masyaf]].
nizari-ismailis-of-syria.r: The castles formed a small state led by a chief missionary appointed from [[e:alamut|Alamut]]. [[e:rashid-al-din-sinan|Rashid al-Din Sinan]], the original Old Man of the Mountain, led it from about 1162 to 1193, making it largely independent. The [[e:nizari-ismailism|Nizaris]] used targeted killings by devotees against powerful enemies, including [[e:conrad-of-montferrat|Conrad of Montferrat]] in 1192, and twice attempted to kill [[e:saladin|Saladin]]. They also paid tribute to the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Hospitallers]] at times.
nizari-ismailis-of-syria.e: After the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] destroyed [[e:alamut|Alamut]] in 1256, the Syrian castles survived, but the [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] sultan [[e:baybars|Baybars]] took them one by one between 1270 and 1273. The [[e:nizari-ismailism|Nizari]] community remained in the region, notably around [[e:salamiyah|Salamiyah]] and [[e:masyaf|Masyaf]].

nongstoin-state.t: The largest of the Khasi states by area, covering much of the West Khasi Hills of present-day Meghalaya.
nongstoin-state.o: Hima Nongstoin was one of the Khasi chiefdoms of the [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]] plateau; its origins are known from oral tradition, and the register's start date is approximate.
nongstoin-state.r: Nongstoin was ruled by a [[e:syiem|Syiem]] chosen from a royal clan by clan heads, with succession through the female line. Its lands were wide but thinly populated, with villages of [[e:rice|rice]] farmers and forest. Little written record exists before the 19th century.
nongstoin-state.e: Nongstoin came under British supervision in the 19th century and acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1948, joining [[e:assam|Assam]]. It is now part of West Khasi Hills district, [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]].

naxos-sicily.t: The first Greek colony in Sicily, founded by Chalcidians in 734 BCE beneath Mount Etna and destroyed by Dionysius I in 403 BCE.
naxos-sicily.o: According to [[e:thucydides|Thucydides]], Chalcidians from [[e:euboea|Euboea]] led by [[e:theocles|Theocles]] founded [[s:naxos|Naxos]] in 734 BCE on the Schisò headland below modern [[e:taormina|Taormina]]; later writers add settlers from the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] island of Naxos, which gave the city its name. As the first landfall for ships crossing from [[e:greece|Greece]], it became the starting point for Greek colonisation of the island.
naxos-sicily.r: [[s:naxos|Naxos]] was small but symbolically important: its altar of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] Archegetes, 'the Founder', was where envoys sailing from [[e:sicily|Sicily]] to [[e:greece|Greece]] made sacrifice. Within a few years it sent out settlers to found [[s:leontini|Leontini]] and [[s:catana|Catana]]. It grew vines on the slopes of [[e:mount-etna|Etna]], and its coins with [[e:dionysus|Dionysus]] and a satyr are celebrated. [[e:hippocrates-of-gela|Hippocrates of Gela]] subdued it around 495 BCE, and later it was often allied with [[s:athens|Athens]] and Leontini against [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]].
naxos-sicily.e: [[e:dionysius-i-of-syracuse|Dionysius I]] captured [[s:naxos|Naxos]] by treachery in 403 BCE, sold its people into [[e:slavery|slavery]] and gave its land to the [[e:sicels|Sicels]]. In 358 BCE survivors and Sicels founded [[s:tauromenium|Tauromenium]] on the hill above. Excavations at [[e:giardini-naxos|Giardini Naxos]] have revealed the walls, sanctuaries and street grid.

nasamones.t: A Libyan people of the Gulf of Sirte described by Herodotus, whose resistance to Roman taxation ended in their near destruction.
nasamones.o: The Nasamones are known almost entirely from Greek and Roman writers. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]], in the 5th century BCE, places them on the shores of the [[e:gulf-of-sirte|Greater Syrtis]], after they took over the lands of the [[e:psylli|Psylli]]. They were herders who each summer travelled inland to the [[e:awjila|Augila]] oasis to harvest dates.
nasamones.r: [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] describes their customs, including swearing oaths at the tombs of respected ancestors and consulting dreams by sleeping on graves. He also tells of five young Nasamonian men who crossed the [[e:sahara|Sahara]] and reached a great river with crocodiles, possibly the [[e:niger-river|Niger]]. Later writers say they plundered ships wrecked on the [[e:gulf-of-sirte|Syrtis]] shoals.
nasamones.e: In 85 to 86 CE the Nasamones rose against Roman tax collectors and defeated the governor of [[s:numidia|Numidia]], but were then crushed by the [[s:roman-empire|Roman Empire]], and [[e:domitian|Domitian]] boasted that he had forbidden them to exist. Survivors were absorbed by other Libyan groups.

neutral-confederacy.t: A populous Iroquoian confederacy north of Lake Erie, named Neutral by the French for staying out of the Huron-Iroquois wars until its own destruction in 1651.
neutral-confederacy.o: The Neutral, called Attawandaron by the [[s:huron-confederacy|Huron]], developed from Iroquoian farming communities in what is now south-western [[e:ontario|Ontario]], between the [[e:grand-river-ontario|Grand River]] and the [[e:niagara-river|Niagara River]]. By the early 17th century they numbered perhaps 30,000 to 40,000 people in around 40 villages, organised as a confederacy of several tribes.
neutral-confederacy.r: French observers named them the Neutral Nation because they let both the [[s:huron-confederacy|Huron Confederacy]] and the [[s:iroquois-confederacy|Iroquois Confederacy]] pass through their lands in peace. They grew [[e:maize|maize]] and tobacco, quarried chert on the [[e:niagara-escarpment|Niagara Escarpment]], and traded with both sides. Under the war chief [[e:tsouharissen|Tsouharissen]] in the 1640s they waged campaigns against Algonquian peoples to the west, notably the [[e:mascouten|Mascouten]]. [[e:recollects|Recollet]] and [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] missionaries, among them [[e:jean-de-brebeuf|Jean de Brébeuf]] in 1640 to 1641, made few converts.
neutral-confederacy.e: After the fall of the [[s:huron-confederacy|Huron]], the [[s:iroquois-confederacy|Iroquois Confederacy]] attacked the Neutral in 1650 and 1651, burning their towns. Thousands were killed or taken captive, and most survivors were absorbed into the [[s:seneca-nation|Seneca]].

nanzan.t: The southernmost of the three rival kingdoms of 14th-century Okinawa, absorbed into the unified Ryukyu Kingdom in 1429.
nanzan.o: [[e:okinawa-island|Okinawa]] split in the early 14th century into three rival polities, [[s:hokuzan|Hokuzan]], [[s:chuzan|Chuzan]] and Nanzan, as local lords called aji built stone castles (gusuku). Nanzan covered the southern part of the island, with its seat at [[e:shimajiri-ozato-castle|Shimajiri-Ozato]] castle; the date of 1314 is traditional.
nanzan.r: Nanzan's kings were overlords of local aji rather than rulers of a centralised state. From 1380 they sent tribute missions to [[e:ming-empire|Ming China]], gaining trade privileges and recognition as kings of Shannan, though succession disputes were frequent.
nanzan.e: [[e:sho-hashi|Sho Hashi]], who had taken control of [[s:chuzan|Chuzan]], conquered Nanzan in 1429, defeating its last king [[e:taromai|Taromai]] and uniting [[e:okinawa-island|Okinawa]] as the [[s:ryukyu-kingdom|Ryukyu Kingdom]].

nagas-of-padmavati.t: A Naga dynasty of central India, ruling from Padmavati near Gwalior between the Kushans and the Guptas.
nagas-of-padmavati.o: After the decline of the [[s:kushan-empire|Kushan Empire]], several Naga ruling families emerged in central and northern [[e:india|India]] in the 2nd and 3rd centuries. The best known ruled from [[e:pawaya|Padmavati]], modern Pawaya near [[s:gwalior-state|Gwalior]], with other branches at [[e:vidisha|Vidisha]] and [[e:mathura|Mathura]]. Many scholars identify them with the Bharashivas of Vakataka records.
nagas-of-padmavati.r: The Nagas are known from many small [[e:copper|copper]] coins and a few inscriptions. Vakataka inscriptions say the Bharashiva kings carried a [[e:shiva|Shiva]] linga on their shoulders and performed ten horse sacrifices and were anointed with the waters of the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]], suggesting strong [[e:shaivism|Shaiva]] devotion. [[e:bhava-naga|Bhava Naga]] married his daughter to the Vakataka house, and his grandson [[e:rudrasena-i|Rudrasena I]] became a Vakataka king.
nagas-of-padmavati.e: In the 4th century [[e:samudragupta|Samudragupta]] of the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]] defeated Naga rulers, including [[e:ganapati-naga|Ganapati Naga]] and [[e:nagasena|Nagasena]], and absorbed their lands. The [[e:gupta-empire|Guptas]] then married into the Naga family through [[e:chandragupta-ii|Chandragupta II's]] queen [[e:kuberanaga|Kuberanaga]].

nanyue.t: The kingdom founded by the Qin general Zhao Tuo in Guangdong and northern Vietnam, which blended Chinese and Yue ways and defied the Han for nearly a century.
nanyue.o: [[e:zhao-tuo|Zhao Tuo]] was a [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] officer sent south in the conquest of the [[e:baiyue|Baiyue]] lands. As the [[s:qin-dynasty|Qin dynasty]] collapsed, he sealed the mountain passes, killed officials loyal to Qin and in 204 BCE proclaimed himself King of Nanyue, with his capital at [[e:guangzhou|Panyu]] (Guangzhou). He later annexed [[s:au-lac|Au Lac]] in the [[e:red-river-asia|Red River]] delta.
nanyue.r: [[e:zhao-tuo|Zhao Tuo]] adopted Yue customs, married into local elites and ruled a mixed population of northern settlers and Yue peoples. He accepted Han overlordship in 196 BCE but styled himself emperor at home. The tomb of his grandson [[e:zhao-mo|Zhao Mo]] in [[e:guangzhou|Guangzhou]], with its jade burial suit and seals, shows a court combining Han, Chu and Yue traditions. In Vietnamese history the line is the Trieu dynasty.
nanyue.e: In 112 BCE the chief minister [[e:lu-jia|Lü Jia]] killed the young king and the pro-Han queen dowager. The [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] sent fleets and armies, and in 111 BCE [[e:guangzhou|Panyu]] fell and Nanyue was divided into [[e:commandery|commanderies]], beginning a millennium of Chinese rule in northern [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]].
nanyue.re: Chinese ancestral religion and Yue local cults

neustria.t: Western kingdom of the Merovingian Franks, centred on Paris and Soissons, and the long rival of Austrasia.
neustria.o: Neustria, the new western land, took shape after the division of 561, when [[e:chilperic-i|Chilperic I]] received [[e:soissons|Soissons]] and the lands between the [[e:loire|Loire]] and the [[e:scheldt|Scheldt]]. It later included [[e:paris|Paris]], [[e:rouen|Rouen]] and [[e:tours|Tours]].
neustria.r: [[e:chilperic-i|Chilperic]] and his queen [[e:fredegund|Fredegund]] waged a bitter feud with Austrasia's [[e:sigebert-i|Sigebert I]] and [[e:brunhilda-of-austrasia|Brunhild]]. Their son [[e:chlothar-ii|Chlothar II]] reunited the [[e:frankish-kingdom|Frankish kingdoms]] in 613. Neustria had a strongly Gallo-Roman population and rich abbeys such as [[e:basilica-of-saint-denis|Saint-Denis]], and in the 7th century its mayor [[e:ebroin|Ebroin]] dominated politics.
neustria.e: The Austrasian [[e:pippin-of-herstal|Pippin of Herstal]] defeated the Neustrians at [[e:battle-of-tertry|Tertry]] in 687, and [[e:charles-martel|Charles Martel]] finally crushed the Neustrian mayor [[e:ragenfrid|Ragenfrid]] in 717 to 719. After 751 Neustria became a region of the Carolingian realm, and the name was later applied to the land between the [[e:seine|Seine]] and the [[e:loire|Loire]].

naranjo.t: A Classic Maya kingdom in eastern Petén, called Sa'al, revived in the 7th century by Lady Six Sky, a princess from Dos Pilas.
naranjo.o: Naranjo grew in the hills between the [[e:peten|Petén]] lakes and the [[s:belize|Belize]] valley. Its dynasty claimed great antiquity, and by the 6th century, around 500 CE, its kings were regional powers, allied at times with [[s:tikal|Tikal]] and at others with the [[s:kingdom-of-kaan|Kingdom of Kaan]].
naranjo.r: Under [[e:aj-wosal-chan-kinich|Aj Wosal]] Naranjo was a client of Kaan, but in the 620s and 630s [[s:caracol|Caracol]] defeated it. In 682 [[e:lady-six-sky|Lady Six Sky]] (Ix Wak Jalam Chan Ajaw), daughter of [[e:bajlaj-chan-kawiil|B'ajlaj Chan K'awiil]] of [[s:dos-pilas|Dos Pilas]], arrived to restore the dynasty. She acted as ruler for her young son [[e:kahk-tiliw-chan-chaak|K'ahk' Tiliw Chan Chaak]], who fought wars against [[s:yaxha|Yaxha]], [[e:ucanal|Ucanal]] and other neighbours. Naranjo was also a centre of fine painted pottery.
naranjo.e: Naranjo's last known monument dates to about 820, after which it declined in the Classic collapse. Heavy looting of its stelae in the 20th century prompted protection; it now lies within the [[e:yaxha-nakum-naranjo-national-park|Yaxha-Nakum-Naranjo National Park]].

nyungu-ya-mawes-state.t: A short-lived conquest state in central Tanzania, built by the Nyamwezi warlord Nyungu ya Mawe with ruga-ruga gunmen.
nyungu-ya-mawes-state.o: [[e:nyungu-ya-mawe|Nyungu ya Mawe]], a member of the ruling family of [[s:unyanyembe|Unyanyembe]], broke with his kin and the Arab traders of [[e:tabora|Tabora]] in the 1860s. From around 1870 he led bands of ruga-ruga to conquer the chiefdoms of Ukimbu, south of Tabora, and established his base at Kiwele.
nyungu-ya-mawes-state.r: Unlike most Nyamwezi chiefs, [[e:nyungu-ya-mawe|Nyungu]] ruled through appointed officials, the vatwale, rather than hereditary chiefs, creating an unusually centralised state. His power rested on firearms and control of the [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] to the south, which he raided or taxed. He controlled a large area of Ukimbu until his death.
nyungu-ya-mawes-state.e: [[e:nyungu-ya-mawe|Nyungu ya Mawe]] died in 1884. His daughter Mgalula held the state together for some years, and it was absorbed into [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]] in the 1890s.

norse-greenland.t: Europe's most remote medieval society, the Norse farming settlements in south-west Greenland that lasted almost five centuries and then vanished.
norse-greenland.o: [[e:erik-the-red|Erik the Red]], outlawed from [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]], led settlers to [[e:greenland|Greenland]] around 985, founding the [[e:eastern-settlement|Eastern Settlement]] near modern [[e:qaqortoq|Qaqortoq]] and a smaller Western Settlement near [[e:nuuk|Nuuk]]. His son [[e:leif-erikson|Leif Erikson]] sailed from Greenland to [[e:north-america|North America]] around 1000 and is credited with bringing [[e:christianity|Christianity]].
norse-greenland.r: The colonists raised [[e:cattle|cattle]], sheep and goats and hunted seals and caribou. Their key export was walrus [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], sent to [[e:europe|Europe]] through [[e:norway|Norway]]. They held their own assembly, and from 1126 a [[e:bishop|bishop]] lived at [[e:gardar-greenland|Garðar]]. In 1261 the Greenlanders accepted the overlordship of the Norwegian king, joining the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]].
norse-greenland.e: The Western Settlement was abandoned in the mid-14th century, and the last written record from the [[e:eastern-settlement|Eastern Settlement]] is a wedding at [[e:hvalsey-church|Hvalsey]] church in 1408. By about 1450 the Norse had disappeared, probably owing to colder climate, falling [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] prices, isolation and emigration. [[e:inuit|Inuit]], who had arrived from the 13th century, remained.

novgorod-republic.t: Lord Novgorod the Great, a merchant republic of the Russian north that hired and fired its princes and traded furs with the Hanseatic League.
novgorod-republic.o: [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] on the [[e:volkhov-river|Volkhov]] had long been the second city of [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']], usually governed by a son of the Kievan prince. In 1136 its citizens expelled Prince [[e:vsevolod-mstislavich|Vsevolod Mstislavich]], and from then on they chose their own princes under contract, limiting them to military command. Historians date the republic from this event.
novgorod-republic.r: Power lay with the town assembly, the veche, the elected posadnik and tysyatsky, the boyar families and the archbishop. [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] controlled a huge northern hinterland reaching to the [[e:white-sea|White Sea]] and the [[e:ural-mountains|Urals]], exporting [[e:fur-trade|furs]], wax and walrus [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] to the Hanseatic merchants of the [[e:peterhof-novgorod|Peterhof]]. Hundreds of birchbark letters show widespread literacy. Its prince [[e:alexander-nevsky|Alexander Nevsky]] defeated the Swedes in 1240 and the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Knights]] in 1242.
novgorod-republic.e: [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] sought Lithuanian help against the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]], a party led by the boyar widow [[e:marfa-boretskaya|Marfa Boretskaya]]. [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III]] crushed its army at the [[e:battle-of-shelon|Shelon]] in 1471, annexed the city in 1478 and carried off the veche bell. Its leading families were deported and the Hanseatic office was closed in 1494.
novgorod-republic.la: Old Novgorod dialect of Old East Slavic

novantae.t: People of Galloway in south-west Scotland, named by Ptolemy, whose peninsula and towns faced the Irish Sea.
novantae.o: Ptolemy lists the Novantae in south-western [[e:scotland|Scotland]], giving their name to a peninsula, the Novantarum Promontorium, usually identified with the [[e:rhins-of-galloway|Rhins of Galloway]], and naming two towns, Locopibia and Rerigonium. They grew from [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] communities living in duns, crannogs and small forts along the coast and inland valleys of [[s:lordship-of-galloway|Galloway]].
novantae.r: No rulers or written records survive. [[e:gnaeus-julius-agricola|Agricola's]] campaigns of about 81 probably brought Roman troops into [[s:lordship-of-galloway|Galloway]], and forts were built at Glenlochar and Gatehouse of Fleet. Their position on the [[e:irish-sea|Irish Sea]] gave them close contact with Ireland and the [[s:isle-of-man|Isle of Man]], and their society was rural and pastoral.
novantae.e: Roman control of the region was brief, and the Novantae disappear from the written record after Ptolemy. Their territory later formed part of British kingdoms of the north, possibly [[s:kingdom-of-rheged|Rheged]], before Northumbrian expansion into [[s:lordship-of-galloway|Galloway]] in the 7th and 8th centuries.

north-borneo.t: Territory in northern Borneo governed by a British chartered company, the last of its kind, until 1946.
north-borneo.o: In 1877 and 1878 the Austrian consul [[e:gustav-von-overbeck|Baron von Overbeck]] and the British merchant [[e:alfred-dent|Alfred Dent]] obtained grants of northern [[e:borneo|Borneo]] from the [[s:brunei-sultanate|Brunei Sultanate]] and the [[s:sulu-sultanate|Sulu Sultanate]]. Dent bought out his partner, and in 1881 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] chartered the [[e:british-north-borneo-company|British North Borneo Company]] to govern the land. It became a British [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1888.
north-borneo.r: The company ruled through a governor at [[e:sandakan|Sandakan]] and a small staff, raising money from land concessions, [[e:timber|timber]], tobacco and later [[e:rubber|rubber]], and taxing trade. It built a railway and brought in Chinese labourers. Local resistance, notably the rebellion of [[e:mat-salleh|Mat Salleh]] from 1894 to 1900, was suppressed, and indigenous peoples such as the [[e:kadazan-dusun|Kadazan-Dusun]] and [[e:murut|Murut]] faced new taxes.
north-borneo.e: [[e:japan|Japan]] occupied the territory from 1942; the [[e:sandakan|Sandakan]] death marches of 1945 killed thousands of Allied prisoners. Ruined by war, the company sold its rights to the British crown in 1946, creating the [[s:crown-colony-of-north-borneo|Crown Colony of North Borneo]].

nadruvians.t: Prussian people of Nadruvia, between the Pregolya and Neman rivers, among the last to be conquered by the Teutonic Knights.
nadruvians.o: Nadruvia lay in the north-east of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], south of the [[e:neman|Neman]], in what is now the [[e:kaliningrad-oblast|Kaliningrad]] region. Its people were [[e:old-prussians|Prussians]], known mainly from [[e:peter-of-dusburg|Peter of Dusburg's]] chronicle, which describes a sacred site called [[e:romowe|Romowe]] somewhere in the territory, though its existence is debated.
nadruvians.r: They lived from farming, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and forest resources, under local nobles with hillforts. Their land bordered [[s:scalovians|Scalovia]] and [[s:sudovians|Sudovia]] and was close to [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]].
nadruvians.e: After defeating the [[e:great-prussian-uprising|Great Prussian Uprising]], the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] conquered Nadruvia in 1274-1277. Much of the population fled or was resettled, and the region became a thinly peopled frontier of the Order's state, later repopulated by [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]] and Germans.

north-german-confederation.t: Prussian-led federal state formed after the defeat of Austria in 1866, the direct forerunner of the German Empire.
north-german-confederation.o: [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia's]] victory in the [[e:austro-prussian-war|Austro-Prussian War]] of 1866 dissolved the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]]. Prussia annexed [[e:hanover|Hanover]], [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]], [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] and [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] and joined the remaining states north of the Main in a new federation. Its constitution, drafted largely by [[e:otto-von-bismarck|Otto von Bismarck]], came into force on 1 July 1867.
north-german-confederation.r: The King of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] held the federal presidency and commanded the armies, and Bismarck was federal chancellor. A [[e:bundesrat-german-empire|Federal Council]] represented the governments, and a [[e:reichstag|Reichstag]] was elected by [[e:universal-suffrage|universal male suffrage]]. The confederation unified weights and measures, trade law and criminal law, and the south German states were tied to it by military alliances and the [[e:customs-union|customs union]].
north-german-confederation.e: During the [[e:franco-prussian-war|Franco-Prussian War]], [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], Württemberg, [[e:baden|Baden]] and [[e:hesse|Hesse]] joined in 1870. The confederation was renamed the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]], and [[e:wilhelm-i|William I]] was proclaimed [[e:german-emperor|German Emperor]] at [[e:versailles|Versailles]] on 18 January 1871.
