netherlands-new-guinea.t: Last Dutch colony in Asia, the western half of New Guinea, whose transfer to Indonesia remains contested by Papuan nationalists.
netherlands-new-guinea.o: When the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] transferred [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] over the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]] in 1949, the status of western [[e:new-guinea|New Guinea]] was left for later talks. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] kept it as Netherlands New Guinea, arguing that its Papuan peoples were culturally distinct from [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]], while [[e:indonesia|Indonesia]] claimed it as part of the former colony.
netherlands-new-guinea.r: Governed from [[e:jayapura|Hollandia]], the colony saw [[e:dutch|Dutch]] investment in schools, missions and administration aimed at preparing Papuans for self-rule. A partly elected [[e:new-guinea|New Guinea]] Council met in 1961, and on 1 December 1961 the Morning Star flag was raised alongside the Dutch flag. Most Papuans lived in villages, and Christian missions had wide influence.
netherlands-new-guinea.e: Under pressure from [[e:sukarno|Sukarno's]] military campaign and the [[s:united-states|United States]], the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] signed the [[e:new-york|New York]] Agreement in August 1962. The territory passed to [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] administration and then to [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]] in 1963, confirmed by the disputed [[e:act-of-free-choice|Act of Free Choice]] in 1969.

northern-zhou.t: The Yuwen family's dynasty in north-western China, which conquered Northern Qi and built the military system that the Sui and Tang inherited.
northern-zhou.o: [[e:yuwen-tai|Yuwen Tai]], the strongman of [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]], had built a powerful army based at [[e:changan|Chang'an]]. After his death in 556 his nephew [[e:yuwen-hu|Yuwen Hu]] forced the last [[e:western-wei|Western Wei]] emperor to abdicate in 557 in favour of [[s:yuwen-xianbei|Yuwen]] Tai's son [[e:yuwen-jue|Yuwen Jue]], who took the archaic title Heavenly King of Zhou.
northern-zhou.r: The regime named its offices after the classical [[e:rites-of-zhou|Rites of Zhou]] to give itself ancient legitimacy, and relied on the [[e:fubing-system|fubing]] militia, which bound [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] and Han soldiers to the state through land grants. [[e:yuwen-hu|Yuwen Hu]] dominated the court until [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]] killed him in 572. Emperor Wu then centralised power, banned [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] and [[e:taoism|Daoism]] in 574 to seize monastic wealth and manpower, and conquered [[s:northern-qi|Northern Qi]] in 577.
northern-zhou.e: [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]] died in 578 and his son [[e:emperor-xuan-of-northern-zhou|Emperor Xuan]] ruled erratically. When the child Emperor Jing succeeded, the regent [[e:emperor-wen-of-sui|Yang Jian]], father of Emperor Xuan's empress, crushed opposition and took the throne in 581 as founder of the [[s:sui-dynasty|Sui Dynasty]].

neutral-moresnet.t: A tiny wedge-shaped territory between Belgium and Prussia, left jointly governed for a century because neither side would give up its zinc mine.
neutral-moresnet.o: After 1815, the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] could not agree on the border near [[s:free-imperial-city-of-aachen|Aachen]] because both wanted the valuable [[e:vieille-montagne|Vieille Montagne]] zinc mine at [[e:kelmis|Kelmis]]. In 1816 they left a small triangle of land under joint administration, with [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] taking the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] role after 1830.
neutral-moresnet.r: Neutral Moresnet was run by a mayor and two royal commissioners, one from each neighbour. Its residents paid low taxes and avoided conscription, and the [[e:vieille-montagne|Vieille Montagne]] company dominated the economy. After the mine was exhausted in 1885, enthusiasts promoted it as a possible [[e:esperanto|Esperanto]] state called Amikejo, and the territory became known for its gambling and distillery.
neutral-moresnet.e: The [[e:treaty-of-versailles|Treaty of Versailles]] of 1919 assigned the territory to the [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Kingdom of Belgium]], effective in 1920. [[e:kelmis|Kelmis]], its main village, is now part of [[e:belgium|Belgium's]] German-speaking community.

nobosohphoh-state.t: A small Khasi chiefdom of the Meghalaya plateau, one of the 25 Khasi states that acceded to India in 1948.
nobosohphoh-state.o: Hima Nobosohphoh was one of the Khasi chiefdoms of the plateau; its origins are known only from oral tradition, and the register's start date is approximate.
nobosohphoh-state.r: Nobosohphoh was headed by a [[e:syiem|Syiem]] chosen from a royal clan, with succession through the female line and decisions taken with clan elders. Little written record of its history exists.
nobosohphoh-state.e: Nobosohphoh came under British supervision in the 19th century and acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1948, joining [[e:assam|Assam]]. It is now part of [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]].

north-western-rhodesia.t: The British South Africa Company territory west of the Kafue, built on treaties with the Lozi king Lewanika.
north-western-rhodesia.o: The [[e:lozi-people|Lozi]] king [[e:lewanika|Lewanika]] of [[s:barotseland|Barotseland]], seeking protection against the [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele]] and Portuguese, signed concessions with agents of the [[e:british-south-africa-company|British South Africa Company]] in 1890 and later. In 1899 an Order in Council created Barotziland-North-Western [[s:rhodesia|Rhodesia]] under company administration, with its capital at [[e:kalomo|Kalomo]].
north-western-rhodesia.r: The administrator [[e:robert-coryndon|Robert Coryndon]] and his successors ruled through [[e:lewanika|Lewanika]], who kept considerable authority in the [[e:lozi-people|Barotse]] heartland. The railway from [[e:bulawayo|Bulawayo]] crossed the [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]] Falls bridge in 1905 and reached the Broken Hill mine in 1906. The capital moved to [[e:livingstone-zambia|Livingstone]] in 1907. Hut tax pushed men to work in Southern Rhodesian mines.
north-western-rhodesia.e: In 1911 North-Western [[s:rhodesia|Rhodesia]] was merged with [[s:north-eastern-rhodesia|North-Eastern Rhodesia]] to form [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]], still under company rule, with [[e:livingstone-zambia|Livingstone]] as capital. [[s:barotseland|Barotseland]] kept a special status that continued into independent [[e:zambia|Zambia]].

natangians.t: Prussian people of Natangia whose leader Herkus Monte led the Great Prussian Uprising against the Teutonic Order from 1260.
natangians.o: Natangia lay south of the [[e:pregolya|Pregolya]] river in central [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], divided today between [[e:russia|Russia's]] [[e:kaliningrad-oblast|Kaliningrad]] region and [[e:poland|Poland]]. Its people were [[e:old-prussians|Prussians]] organised in districts under nobles, known from [[e:peter-of-dusburg|Peter of Dusburg's]] chronicle.
natangians.r: The Natangians farmed fertile land and defended themselves from hillforts. The [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] first subdued them around 1240, but they kept their nobility and pagan beliefs under thin Christian rule. [[e:herkus-monte|Herkus Monte]], a Natangian noble educated in [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]], became the most famous Prussian leader.
natangians.e: After the Order's defeat at [[e:battle-of-durbe|Durbe]] in 1260, [[e:herkus-monte|Herkus Monte]] led the [[e:great-prussian-uprising|Great Prussian Uprising]], winning at [[e:battle-of-pokarwis|Pokarwis]] in 1261. He was captured and hanged in 1273, and by 1274 the Natangians were defeated. Natangia became part of the Order's state and, later, of [[s:duchy-of-prussia|Ducal Prussia]].

natchez-chiefdom.t: The last Mississippian-style chiefdom of the Lower Mississippi, ruled by the sacred Great Sun until its war with the French in 1729.
natchez-chiefdom.o: The Natchez descended from the Plaquemine culture of the Lower [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] Valley. [[e:emerald-mound|Emerald Mound]], one of the largest platform mounds in [[e:north-america|North America]], was built from around 1250, and by the late 17th century the political centre was the [[e:grand-village-of-the-natchez|Grand Village]] on St Catherine [[e:muscogee|Creek]], near the modern city of Natchez, Mississippi.
natchez-chiefdom.r: The [[e:great-sun|Great Sun]], a sacred ruler said to descend from the sun, lived on a mound facing a temple where an eternal fire burned. Society was divided into Suns, Nobles, Honoured People and commoners, and members of the upper ranks had to marry commoners, so rank shifted through the female line. When the war chief [[e:tattooed-serpent|Tattooed Serpent]] died in 1725, wives and retainers were killed to accompany him, as described by the French settler [[e:antoine-simon-le-page-du-pratz|Le Page du Pratz]]. The Natchez farmed [[e:maize|maize]] and spoke a language isolate.
natchez-chiefdom.e: [[s:french-louisiana|French Louisiana]] built [[e:fort-rosalie|Fort Rosalie]] in 1716. In 1729 the Natchez attacked it, killing around 230 colonists. French and [[s:choctaw-nation|Choctaw]] forces retaliated, and by 1731 hundreds of Natchez, including the [[e:great-sun|Great Sun]], had been sold into [[e:slavery|slavery]] in [[s:saint-domingue|Saint-Domingue]]. Survivors joined the [[s:chickasaw-nation|Chickasaw]], [[e:muscogee|Muscogee]] and [[e:cherokee|Cherokee]].

northern-han.t: The last of the Ten Kingdoms, a Liao-backed Shatuo state at Taiyuan that held out against the Song until 979.
northern-han.o: When [[e:guo-wei|Guo Wei]] overthrew the [[s:later-han|Later Han]] in 951, [[e:liu-chong|Liu Chong]], brother of its founder [[e:liu-zhiyuan|Liu Zhiyuan]] and governor of [[e:hedong-shanxi|Hedong]], proclaimed himself emperor at [[e:taiyuan|Taiyuan]], refusing to recognise the [[s:later-zhou|Later Zhou]] and claiming to continue the [[e:han-dynasty|Han dynasty]].
northern-han.r: Northern Han held only the poor, mountainous centre of [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]] and depended on the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]], whose emperor [[e:liu-chong|Liu Chong]] addressed as 'uncle' and paid tribute. Its army was strong in defence, but it could not afford long wars. With Khitan help it attacked [[s:later-zhou|Later Zhou]] in 954 and was beaten at [[e:battle-of-gaoping|Gaoping]].
northern-han.e: The [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]] attacked [[e:taiyuan|Taiyuan]] in 968 and 969, even flooding the city, but [[e:liao-dynasty|Liao]] relief armies saved it. In 979 [[e:emperor-taizong-of-song|Emperor Taizong of Song]] defeated the Khitan relief force and besieged Taiyuan until [[e:liu-jiyuan|Liu Jiyuan]] surrendered. The city was razed, completing the [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] reunification of [[e:china|China]] proper.

nobadia.t: The northernmost Nubian kingdom, heir to Meroë in Lower Nubia and the first to adopt Christianity in the 6th century.
nobadia.o: As the [[s:kushite-empire|Kushite Empire]] of [[e:meroe|Meroë]] collapsed in the 4th century, the Noubades ([[e:nobades|Nobatae]]), a people settled in [[e:lower-nubia|Lower Nubia]], formed a kingdom between the First and Third Cataracts. Its early rulers, known archaeologically as the [[e:ballana|Ballana]] culture, were buried in great tumuli at Ballana and [[e:qustul|Qustul]] with [[e:silver|silver]] crowns, horses and servants.
nobadia.r: Nobadia's kings received Roman [[e:subsidy|subsidies]] to guard the frontier and fought the [[s:blemmyes|Blemmyes]]; [[e:silko|King Silko]], in a Greek inscription at [[e:kalabsha|Kalabsha]], boasted of driving them from the [[e:nile|Nile]] valley in the 5th century. The capital was [[e:faras|Faras]] (Pachoras). Around 543 a Miaphysite mission led by the priest Julian, backed by Empress [[e:theodora-wife-of-justinian-i|Theodora]], converted the court, and churches, Coptic and Greek literacy followed.
nobadia.e: By around 700 Nobadia was united with [[s:makuria|Makuria]], probably under King [[e:merkurios|Merkurios]], but kept its own governor, the eparch of Nobadia. [[e:faras|Faras]] became a great bishopric whose cathedral paintings are now in [[e:warsaw|Warsaw]] and [[e:khartoum|Khartoum]].

northern-rhodesia.t: The British protectorate on the Zambezi built around the Copperbelt, which became independent Zambia.
northern-rhodesia.o: In 1911 the [[e:british-south-africa-company|British South Africa Company]] merged [[s:north-western-rhodesia|North-Western Rhodesia]] and [[s:north-eastern-rhodesia|North-Eastern Rhodesia]] into Northern Rhodesia, with its capital at [[e:livingstone-zambia|Livingstone]]. In 1924 the [[e:colonial-office|Colonial Office]] took over administration, though the company kept the mineral rights until 1964.
northern-rhodesia.r: From the late 1920s the [[e:copperbelt|Copperbelt]] grew into one of the world's leading [[e:copper|copper]] producers, drawing African workers whose strikes in 1935 and 1940 were early signs of organised protest. The capital moved to [[e:lusaka|Lusaka]] in 1935. [[s:barotseland|Barotseland]] kept a protected status under its [[e:lozi-people|Lozi]] king. Settlers were few but sought amalgamation with [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]].
northern-rhodesia.e: The territory was joined to the [[s:federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland|Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland]] in 1953. Opposition led by [[e:harry-nkumbula|Harry Nkumbula]] and [[e:kenneth-kaunda|Kenneth Kaunda's]] [[e:united-national-independence-party|United National Independence Party]] ended the federation, and Northern Rhodesia became independent as [[e:zambia|Zambia]] on 24 October 1964 with Kaunda as president.

northern-yuan.t: The Mongol dynasty that continued on the steppe after being driven out of China in 1368, outlasting the Ming's attempts to destroy it for nearly three centuries.
northern-yuan.o: In 1368 [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]] armies approached [[e:dadu|Dadu]], and [[e:toghon-temur|Toghon Temür]], last emperor of the [[s:yuan-dynasty|Yuan Dynasty]], fled to [[e:shangdu|Shangdu]] and then to [[e:yingchang|Yingchang]]. His son [[e:ayushiridara|Ayushiridara]] re-established the court at [[e:karakorum|Karakorum]], still claiming rule over all [[e:china|China]], and his generals defeated a [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] invasion of [[s:mongolia|Mongolia]] in 1372.
northern-yuan.r: The khans ruled a shifting federation of Mongol and [[e:oirats|Oirat]] [[e:tumen|tumens]] rather than a centralised state. After a [[e:ming-empire|Ming]] victory at [[e:battle-of-buyur-lake|Lake Buir]] in 1388, power fragmented, and the [[s:four-oirat|Four Oirat]] often dominated; their leader [[e:esen-taishi|Esen]] captured the Ming emperor at [[e:tumu-crisis|Tumu]] in 1449. [[e:dayan-khan|Dayan Khan]] reunited the eastern [[e:mongols|Mongols]] around 1500 into six tumens, and from the 1570s [[e:tibetan-buddhism|Tibetan Buddhism]] spread under [[e:altan-khan|Altan Khan]].
northern-yuan.e: [[e:ligdan-khan|Ligdan Khan]], the last great khan, tried to restore central power but was defeated by the [[e:manchus|Manchus]] and died in 1634. In 1635 his son Ejei surrendered with the Yuan imperial seal to [[e:hong-taiji|Hong Taiji]] of the [[s:later-jin-1616-1636|Later Jin]] (1616-1636), who soon founded the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]].

northern-court.t: The line of Japanese emperors in Kyoto backed by the Ashikaga shoguns during the 14th-century schism, from whom the present imperial family descends.
northern-court.o: When [[e:emperor-go-daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] broke with [[e:ashikaga-takauji|Ashikaga Takauji]], Takauji placed [[e:emperor-komyo|Komyo]], of the rival [[e:jimyoin-line|Jimyoin]] branch of the imperial house, on the throne in [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] in 1336. Go-Daigo fled with the sacred regalia to [[e:yoshino-nara|Yoshino]], splitting the court in two.
northern-court.r: The Northern Court depended on Ashikaga military power and had little independent authority, but it held the capital and conducted court ceremonies and appointments. Its emperors included [[e:emperor-komyo|Komyo]], [[e:emperor-suko|Suko]], [[e:emperor-go-kogon|Go-Kogon]], [[e:emperor-go-enyu|Go-En'yu]] and [[e:emperor-go-komatsu|Go-Komatsu]]. During the [[e:kanno-disturbance|Kanno disturbance]] of 1350 to 1352 Southern forces seized [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] and carried off three Northern ex-emperors.
northern-court.e: In 1392 [[e:ashikaga-yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]] negotiated reunification: the Southern emperor handed the regalia to [[e:emperor-go-komatsu|Go-Komatsu]], ending the schism. In 1911 the Meiji government declared the [[s:southern-court|Southern Court]] legitimate, though later emperors descend from the Northern line.

northern-liang.t: The Hexi Corridor kingdom of the Juqu family, a major centre of early Chinese Buddhism, whose survivors carried the state to Turpan after 439.
northern-liang.o: In 397 [[e:juqu-mengxun|Juqu Mengxun]], a Lushuihu [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] chief, rebelled against [[s:later-liang-386-403|Later Liang]] and set up the Chinese official [[e:duan-ye|Duan Ye]] as ruler at [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]] commandery near [[e:zhangye|Zhangye]]. In 401 he killed Duan Ye and took power himself, later moving the capital to [[e:wuwei|Guzang]] (Wuwei) in 412 and conquering [[s:western-liang|Western Liang]] in 421.
northern-liang.r: Northern [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]] was a prosperous [[e:silk-road|Silk Road]] state. [[e:juqu-mengxun|Juqu Mengxun]] was a devout Buddhist who sponsored the translator [[e:dharmakshema|Dharmakshema]], whose version of the [[e:mahaparinirvana-sutra|Mahaparinirvana Sutra]] became influential, and cave temples such as [[e:tiantishan-grottoes|Tiantishan]]. Scholars from Liang later carried Hexi learning to the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] court.
northern-liang.e: [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] captured [[e:wuwei|Guzang]] and [[e:juqu-mujian|Juqu Mujian]] in 439, completing its unification of the north. His brothers [[e:juqu-wuhui|Juqu Wuhui]] and [[e:juqu-anzhou|Juqu Anzhou]] fled west and ruled [[s:gaochang-kingdom|Gaochang]] from 442 until the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran Khaganate]] killed Anzhou in 460.

nicarao-chiefdom.t: The Nahua-speaking chiefdom by Lake Nicaragua whose ruler, Nicarao, gave his name to the country of Nicaragua.
nicarao-chiefdom.o: The Nicarao were Nahua-speaking migrants from central [[s:mexico|Mexico]] who settled the isthmus of [[e:rivas-nicaragua|Rivas]] between [[e:lake-nicaragua|Lake Nicaragua]] and the Pacific, probably in the 12th or 13th century, displacing earlier [[e:chorotega|Chorotega]] groups.
nicarao-chiefdom.r: They were governed by a chief and a council of elders, held markets, and used [[e:cacao|cacao]] beans as currency. Their calendar, religion and language followed central Mexican models. In 1523 the cacique, known to the Spanish as Nicarao, received [[e:gil-gonzalez-davila|Gil González Dávila]] and asked him searching questions about [[e:christianity|Christianity]], the flood and the end of the world before agreeing to baptism.
nicarao-chiefdom.e: [[e:francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-founder-of-nicaragua|Francisco Hernández de Córdoba]] conquered the region in 1524 and founded [[e:granada|Granada]] and León. The Nicarao population collapsed through disease and the export of slaves to [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] and [[e:peru|Peru]]. Their chief's name survives in the name of [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]].

nitiobroges.t: Gallic people of the middle Garonne around Agen, whose king Teutomatus fought for Vercingetorix at Gergovia.
nitiobroges.o: The Nitiobroges lived on the [[e:garonne|Garonne]] around [[e:agen|Aginnum]] (Agen), at the border between the Celtic peoples and the [[e:aquitani|Aquitani]]. Caesar notes that their king [[e:ollovico|Ollovico]] had been honoured by the [[s:commune-of-rome|Roman Senate]] as a friend.
nitiobroges.r: They were ruled by kings in Caesar's day. Their land lay on the river route from the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] to the Atlantic, and their coins circulated widely in south-western [[e:gaul|Gaul]].
nitiobroges.e: [[e:ollovico|Ollovico's]] son [[e:teutomatus|Teutomatus]] joined [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]] in 52 BCE with cavalry raised in [[e:gallia-aquitania|Aquitania]]; during the attack on [[e:gergovia|Gergovia]] he escaped from his tent half-dressed on a wounded horse. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] [[e:agen|Aginnum]] became a civitas capital, the origin of Agen.

niassa-company.t: A Portuguese chartered company that governed northern Mozambique for almost four decades, chiefly as a source of labour and taxes.
niassa-company.o: Lacking the money to occupy northern [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]], Portugal granted a charter in 1891 to the Companhia do Niassa, covering the land between the [[e:ruvuma-river|Rovuma]] and [[e:lurio-river|Lúrio]] rivers from the coast to [[e:lake-malawi|Lake Malawi]]. Much of its capital came from British and South African investors, and its headquarters moved from [[e:ibo-island|Ibo]] to [[e:pemba-mozambique|Porto Amélia]], now Pemba.
niassa-company.r: The company had sovereign powers to tax, build ports and grant land, but invested little. Its revenue came mainly from hut tax and from recruiting workers for South African mines. It conquered the interior only slowly, defeating the [[s:mataka-chiefdom|Mataka Chiefdom]] of the Yao in 1912. During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] German forces from [[e:east-africa|East Africa]] invaded its territory.
niassa-company.e: When its charter expired in 1929, Portugal did not renew it, and the region came under direct administration as part of [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Portuguese Mozambique]]. The company left a reputation for neglect and forced labour.

new-kingdom-of-leon.t: A Spanish frontier province of north-eastern New Spain, founded by the Portuguese-born Luis de Carvajal, from which modern Nuevo León and Monterrey grew.
new-kingdom-of-leon.o: In 1579 the Crown granted [[e:luis-de-carvajal-y-de-la-cueva|Luis de Carvajal y de la Cueva]] a huge territory in the north-east, and he began settling it in 1582. After Carvajal's arrest by the [[e:portuguese-inquisition|Inquisition]], his relatives having been accused of secretly practising [[e:judaism|Judaism]], [[e:diego-de-montemayor|Diego de Montemayor]] refounded [[e:monterrey|Monterrey]] in 1596.
new-kingdom-of-leon.r: The province was a thinly settled frontier of ranches and small mining camps. Settlers relied on [[e:cattle|cattle]] and sheep and on the forced labour of local hunter-gatherers, captured under the congrega system, which provoked frequent resistance. [[e:monterrey|Monterrey]] remained a small town for most of the colonial era, governed by a governor under [[s:new-spain|New Spain]].
new-kingdom-of-leon.e: In 1824, after independence, the province became the state of [[e:nuevo-leon|Nuevo León]] in the [[s:first-mexican-republic|First Mexican Republic]]. [[e:monterrey|Monterrey]] later grew into one of [[e:mexico|Mexico's]] major industrial cities.
ru: Luis de Carvajal y de la Cueva

netherlands-antilles.t: Autonomous country of six Dutch Caribbean islands within the Kingdom of the Netherlands from 1954, dissolved into separate parts in 2010.
netherlands-antilles.o: The Charter for the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Kingdom of the Netherlands]], signed on 15 December 1954, turned the colony of [[s:colony-of-curacao|Curaçao and Dependencies]] into the [[e:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] Antilles, an equal partner with the Netherlands and [[s:suriname|Suriname]]. It comprised [[s:curacao|Curaçao]], [[s:aruba|Aruba]] and [[e:bonaire|Bonaire]] off [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]], and [[s:sint-maarten|Sint Maarten]], Saba and [[s:sint-eustatius|Sint Eustatius]] in the [[e:leeward-islands|Leewards]].
netherlands-antilles.r: The Antilles had their own parliament, the Staten, and government at [[e:willemstad|Willemstad]], while the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] handled defence and foreign affairs. Oil refining on [[s:curacao|Curaçao]] and [[s:aruba|Aruba]], offshore finance and tourism sustained the economy. [[e:papiamento|Papiamentu]], [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and English were spoken. Labour unrest erupted in the Curaçao riots of 30 May 1969, which brought Afro-Curaçaoan politicians to power. Resentment of Curaçao's dominance grew on the smaller islands.
netherlands-antilles.e: [[s:aruba|Aruba]] left in 1986 to become a separate country. On 10 October 2010 the [[e:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] Antilles were dissolved: [[s:curacao|Curaçao]] and [[s:sint-maarten|Sint Maarten]] became countries within the kingdom, and [[e:bonaire|Bonaire]], [[s:sint-eustatius|Sint Eustatius]] and Saba became special municipalities of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]].

nupe-kingdom.t: Kingdom of the Niger valley above the confluence, founded by the hero Tsoede and famed for its glass, brass and cloth.
nupe-kingdom.o: Nupe tradition credits [[e:tsoede|Tsoede]], also called Edegi, a son of the Attah of the [[s:igala-kingdom|Igala Kingdom]] by a Nupe mother, with uniting the Nupe chiefdoms in the early 16th century. Travelling up the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] in a bronze canoe, he founded the capital at Gbara and gave the kingdom its royal regalia.
nupe-kingdom.r: The [[e:etsu-nupe|Etsu Nupe]] ruled over farmers, fishermen and skilled craftsmen whose glass [[e:bead|beads]], brassware and cloth were traded widely. Nupe controlled the river between [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]] and [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] country and fought the [[s:oyo-empire|Oyo Empire]], sometimes paying it tribute and sometimes defeating it. [[e:islam|Islam]] spread among the elite from the 18th century.
nupe-kingdom.e: In the early 19th century rival claimants Majiya and Jimada fought for the throne, and the [[e:fula|Fulani]] cleric [[e:mallam-dendo|Mallam Dendo]] exploited the conflict. His descendants took power, and Nupe was absorbed into the [[s:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]], later as the [[s:bida-emirate|Bida Emirate]]. The [[e:etsu-nupe|Etsu Nupe]] still reigns at [[e:bida|Bida]].

new-france.t: France's North American empire, stretching from the St Lawrence through the Great Lakes to the Gulf of Mexico, and the origin of French-speaking Canada.
new-france.o: [[e:jacques-cartier|Jacques Cartier]] claimed the [[e:gaspe-peninsula|Gaspé]] for [[e:france|France]] in 1534, but lasting settlement began when [[e:samuel-de-champlain|Samuel de Champlain]] founded [[s:province-of-quebec|Quebec]] in 1608 as a fur-trading post. [[e:trois-rivieres|Trois-Rivières]] followed in 1634 and [[e:montreal|Montreal]] in 1642. [[e:chartered-company|Chartered companies]] ran the colony until 1663, when [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] made it a royal province.
new-france.r: A governor handled war and diplomacy, an intendant such as [[e:jean-talon|Jean Talon]] ran finance and justice, and a [[e:bishop|bishop]], beginning with [[e:francois-de-laval|François de Laval]], led a powerful Catholic church. Settlers held land under the seigneurial system, but the economy rested on [[e:fur-trade|furs]] gathered through Native alliances with the [[s:huron-confederacy|Huron Confederacy]] and others. Explorers and traders pushed into the [[e:great-lakes|Great Lakes]], the [[e:illinois-country|Illinois Country]] and [[s:french-louisiana|French Louisiana]]. By 1760 the colony had only around 70,000 settlers.
new-france.e: In the Seven Years War [[s:province-of-quebec|Quebec]] fell in 1759 after the [[e:battle-of-the-plains-of-abraham|Battle of the Plains of Abraham]] and [[e:montreal|Montreal]] in 1760. The [[e:treaty-of-paris-1763|Treaty of Paris]] in 1763 handed [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]] to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] as the Province of [[e:quebec|Quebec]]. [[e:french-language|French language]], law and [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] survived, shaping modern Quebec.

north-sea-empire.t: The short-lived union of England, Denmark and Norway under Cnut the Great, which made the North Sea the centre of an Anglo-Scandinavian realm.
north-sea-empire.o: [[e:cnut-the-great|Cnut]], son of the Danish king [[e:sweyn-forkbeard|Sweyn Forkbeard]], conquered [[e:england|England]] in 1016 after the death of [[e:edmund-ironside|Edmund Ironside]]. He inherited [[e:denmark|Denmark]] from his brother Harald around 1018 and, after driving out [[e:olaf-ii-of-norway|Olaf Haraldsson]], took [[e:norway|Norway]] in 1028, also claiming lordship over part of the Swedes.
north-sea-empire.r: [[e:cnut-the-great|Cnut]] ruled mainly from [[e:england|England]], often from [[e:winchester|Winchester]], keeping English institutions, issuing law codes and marrying [[e:emma-of-normandy|Emma of Normandy]], widow of [[e:aethelred-the-unready|Æthelred the Unready]]. He governed [[e:denmark|Denmark]] and [[e:norway|Norway]] through regents, including his son [[e:harthacnut|Harthacnut]] and the earls of [[e:lade-trondheim|Lade]]. A pilgrimage to [[e:rome|Rome]] in 1027, where he attended [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Conrad II]]'s coronation, raised his standing among Christian rulers.
north-sea-empire.e: [[e:cnut-the-great|Cnut]] died at [[e:shaftesbury|Shaftesbury]] in 1035, and his realm broke apart. [[e:norway|Norway]] rejected Danish rule under [[e:magnus-the-good|Magnus the Good]], while his sons [[e:harold-harefoot|Harold Harefoot]] and [[e:harthacnut|Harthacnut]] divided [[e:england|England]] and [[e:denmark|Denmark]]. After Harthacnut's death in 1042 the English throne returned to [[e:edward-the-confessor|Edward the Confessor]], and the [[s:kingdom-of-denmark|Kingdom of Denmark]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]] went their own ways.

northern-ngoni-kingdom.t: The Ngoni kingdom of Mbelwa in northern Malawi, heirs of Zwangendaba's long migration from Zululand.
northern-ngoni-kingdom.o: The Jere [[e:ngoni|Ngoni]] under [[e:zwangendaba|Zwangendaba]] left the [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]] region in the early 1820s and crossed the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] in 1835. After Zwangendaba's death in about 1848 the group split. One branch, under his son [[e:mbelwa|Mbelwa]], settled in the [[e:mzimba-district|Mzimba]] highlands of northern [[e:malawi|Malawi]] in the 1850s and made it the centre of a new kingdom.
northern-ngoni-kingdom.r: [[e:mbelwa|Mbelwa]] ruled through regiments and a hierarchy of royal villages, with Ekwendeni among the leading centres. Captives from the [[e:tumbuka-people|Tumbuka]], [[s:kingdom-of-tonga|Tonga]] and [[e:chewa|Chewa]] were absorbed, so that the [[e:ngoni|Ngoni]] language gave way to [[e:tumbuka-language|Chitumbuka]]. Raids for [[e:cattle|cattle]] and people were central until Scottish missionaries of the [[e:livingstonia|Livingstonia]] mission won influence from the 1880s.
northern-ngoni-kingdom.e: [[e:mbelwa|Mbelwa]] died in 1891. Persuaded by missionaries, his successors accepted British rule without war in 1904, and the kingdom was incorporated into the [[s:british-central-africa-protectorate|British Central Africa Protectorate]], later [[s:nyasaland|Nyasaland]]; the Mbelwa chieftaincy survives.

nanzhao.t: A kingdom around Lake Erhai in Yunnan that played Tang China and the Tibetan Empire against each other and dominated south-western trade routes for 160 years.
nanzhao.o: Six chiefdoms (zhao) lived around [[e:lake-erhai|Lake Erhai]] in western [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]]. With [[s:later-tang|Tang]] backing, [[e:piluoge|Piluoge]], ruler of the southernmost, Mengshe, united them by 738 and was recognised as Prince of Yunnan. He built his capital at [[e:taihe-nanzhao|Taihe]], and his successors moved to [[e:yangjumie|Yangjumie]], near modern Dali.
nanzhao.r: The Meng kings ruled a mixed population, including ancestors of the Bai and Yi peoples, through Tang-style ministries and military districts. [[e:geluofeng|Geluofeng]] broke with [[s:later-tang|Tang]] and destroyed Chinese armies in 751 and 754 as an ally of [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]]; [[e:yimouxun|Yimouxun]] returned to Tang allegiance in 794. Nanzhao sacked [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] in 829 and raided [[s:protectorate-general-to-pacify-the-south|Annan]] in the 860s. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] grew strongly at court, and Chinese writing was used for administration.
nanzhao.e: Costly wars weakened the monarchy. In 902 the minister [[e:zheng-maisi|Zheng Maisi]] massacred the Meng royal family and founded [[s:da-changhe|Da Changhe]]. The [[e:lake-erhai|Erhai]] basin remained a political centre and passed in time to the [[s:dali-kingdom|Dali Kingdom]].
nanzhao.la: Bai and Yi languages, Middle Chinese for writing

northern-xiongnu.t: The part of the Xiongnu that stayed on the Mongolian steppe after the split of 48 CE, crushed by Han and allied armies in 89 to 91 and driven west.
northern-xiongnu.o: In 48 CE a succession dispute split the [[s:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu Empire]]. The southern chief Bi submitted to the Han, while the shanyu Punu kept the northern tribes on the Mongolian plateau, giving rise to the Northern Xiongnu.
northern-xiongnu.r: The northern shanyus kept the traditional [[e:xiongnu-empire|Xiongnu]] system of a supreme ruler with left and right kings, herding on the steppe and drawing tribute from the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]] oases. They raided the Han frontier and competed with the [[s:southern-xiongnu|Southern Xiongnu]], while drought, locusts and attacks by the [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] and [[s:wuhuan|Wuhuan]] weakened them.
northern-xiongnu.e: In 89 the Han general [[e:dou-xian|Dou Xian]], with [[s:southern-xiongnu|Southern Xiongnu]] and other allies, routed the Northern Xiongnu and carved a victory inscription at Mount Yanran, found in [[s:mongolia|Mongolia]] in 2017. In 91 the shanyu fled west. Remnants survived in [[s:dzungar-khanate|Dzungaria]] until the mid-2nd century, while the [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] took over the steppe; any link to the later [[e:huns|Huns]] remains debated.

ngoenyang.t: The early Tai principality of Chiang Saen in the Golden Triangle, the homeland of King Mangrai, who built it into the kingdom of Lan Na.
ngoenyang.o: Northern Thai chronicles trace Ngoenyang, also called Hiran Ngoenyang, to [[e:lao-chakkaraj|Lao Chakkaraj]], who is said to have founded a dynasty on the upper [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]] in the 7th century, with its seat later at [[e:chiang-saen|Chiang Saen]]. These early dates rest on legend; the principality is better known from the 13th century.
ngoenyang.r: Ngoenyang was one of several Tai muang, small valley principalities based on irrigated [[e:rice|rice]] and ruled by hereditary chiefs with kin ties to neighbouring rulers. Its lords were linked by marriage to [[s:sipsong-panna|Chiang Hung]] in [[e:xishuangbanna|Sipsongpanna]] and to [[e:phayao|Phayao]]. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] was spreading in the region but the earliest history is mostly legendary.
ngoenyang.e: [[e:mangrai|Mangrai]] became ruler around 1259 and expanded southward, founding [[e:chiang-rai|Chiang Rai]] in 1262 and conquering [[s:hariphunchai|Hariphunchai]] in 1292. He moved his capital to [[s:kingdom-of-chiang-mai|Chiang Mai]] in 1296, and Ngoenyang became the core of the kingdom of [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]]. [[e:chiang-saen|Chiang Saen]] remained an important northern city.

nurpur-state.t: The Pathania Rajput hill state whose Rajas served and defied the Mughal emperors, and whose capital Dhameri was renamed Nurpur in honour of Jahangir.
nurpur-state.o: The Pathania [[e:rajputs|Rajputs]] first ruled from [[e:pathankot|Pathankot]] (Paithan) on the edge of the [[e:punjab|Punjab]] plains, and tradition places their origins around 1000. In the 16th century they moved their seat into the hills at Dhameri, which was renamed Nurpur in the early 17th century after the emperor [[e:jahangir|Jahangir]], Nur-ud-din.
nurpur-state.r: Nurpur's Rajas were prominent Mughal commanders. Raja Basu fortified Nurpur and served [[e:akbar|Akbar]] and [[e:jahangir|Jahangir]], while his son [[e:jagat-singh-of-nurpur|Jagat Singh]] campaigned for the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] in [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]] before rebelling against [[e:shah-jahan|Shah Jahan]] in 1641–1642; after a long siege of his forts he was pardoned. The state lay on the route from the plains into [[s:chamba-state|Chamba]] and [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]].
nurpur-state.e: [[e:ranjit-singh|Ranjit Singh]] annexed Nurpur to the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]] in 1815, and Raja Bir Singh died in 1846 while trying to recover it. The area passed to [[s:british-raj|British India]] in 1846 and is now in [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] district, [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]].

cr.a: Surveyed by Alexander Cunningham, drawn by Kalleemoodden

nervii.t: The fiercest of the Belgic peoples, who banned wine and luxuries and almost defeated Caesar at the Battle of the Sabis in 57 BCE.
nervii.o: The Nervii lived in the [[s:county-of-hainaut|Hainaut]] region of modern [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] and northern [[e:france|France]], between the [[e:scheldt|Scheldt]] and the [[e:sambre|Sambre]]. Caesar reports that they forbade merchants and wine, believing luxuries weakened courage, and that they were proud of their Germanic descent.
nervii.r: They had no cavalry to speak of and fought on foot, using thick hedges of bent saplings to block their land against raiders. Their war leader in 57 BCE was [[e:boduognatus|Boduognatus]].
nervii.e: At the [[e:battle-of-the-sabis|Sabis]] (probably the [[e:sambre|Sambre]]) in 57 BCE they surprised Caesar's camp and were crushed only after a desperate battle. In 54 BCE they besieged [[e:quintus-tullius-cicero|Quintus Cicero]]'s winter camp. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their chief town was [[e:bavay|Bagacum]] (Bavay), later [[s:prince-bishopric-of-cambrai|Cambrai]].

nguyen-lords.t: The southern Vietnamese lords who built Dang Trong, pushed Vietnam into the Mekong delta and founded the line of the last imperial dynasty.
nguyen-lords.o: In 1558 [[e:nguyen-hoang|Nguyen Hoang]], son of the Le loyalist leader [[e:nguyen-kim|Nguyen Kim]], had himself appointed governor of [[e:thuan-hoa|Thuan Hoa]] in central [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] to escape the [[s:trinh-lords|Trinh lords]]. He and his successors built an autonomous realm, Dang Trong, Europeans' [[s:french-cochinchina|Cochinchina]], with its capital eventually at [[e:hue|Phu Xuan]], present-day Hue.
nguyen-lords.r: The [[e:nguyen-lords|Nguyen lords]] defended the [[e:dong-hoi|Dong Hoi]] walls against Trinh attacks between 1627 and 1672 with the help of Portuguese [[e:field-artillery|cannon]]. They encouraged settlement south into former [[e:cham|Cham]] and [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] lands, absorbing [[e:panduranga|Panduranga]] and the [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]] delta, and welcomed Chinese Ming loyalists who founded towns such as [[e:my-tho|My Tho]]. Hoi An flourished as an international port.
nguyen-lords.e: In 1771 the [[e:tay-son-dynasty|Tay Son rebellion]] broke out, and by 1777 the Tay Son had killed most of the Nguyen family. A survivor, [[e:gia-long|Nguyen Anh]], fought back from the delta and Siam and in 1802 founded the [[s:nguyen-dynasty|Nguyen dynasty]] as emperor Gia Long.

namayan.t: A confederation of Tagalog settlements on the Pasig River, centred at Sapa in today's Santa Ana district of Manila.
namayan.o: Namayan is known from Spanish Franciscan accounts and from archaeology at [[e:santa-ana-manila|Santa Ana]] church, where burials with Chinese ceramics of the [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] and Ming periods were found. Tradition, recorded centuries later, dates its rise to 1175 and names its early rulers as Lakan Tagkan and his wife Kalangitan. The date and names cannot be confirmed.
namayan.r: Namayan was a loose league of barangays along the [[e:pasig-river|Pasig River]] and the shores of [[e:laguna-de-bay|Laguna de Bay]], linked by kinship and trade. Its people farmed [[e:rice|rice]], fished and traded with Chinese merchants, and like [[s:kingdom-of-tondo|Tondo]] and [[s:kingdom-of-maynila|Maynila]] it was led by a hereditary nobility.
namayan.e: After the Spanish took [[s:kingdom-of-maynila|Maynila]] in 1571 Namayan came under their rule, and in 1578 [[e:franciscans|Franciscans]] founded the mission of [[e:santa-ana-manila|Santa Ana]] de Sapa there. Its lands became the districts of Santa Ana, [[e:pandacan|Pandacan]] and others of modern [[e:manila|Manila]].

nguyen-dynasty.t: Vietnam's last imperial dynasty, which unified the country from Hue in 1802 and ruled under French protection until Bao Dai abdicated in 1945.
nguyen-dynasty.o: [[e:gia-long|Nguyen Anh]], a survivor of the [[s:nguyen-lords|Nguyen lords]], fought the [[s:tay-son-dynasty|Tay Son dynasty]] for over twenty years with Siamese, Chinese and French help, including the missionary [[e:pierre-pigneau-de-behaine|Pigneau de Behaine]]. In 1802 he proclaimed himself emperor Gia Long and took [[e:thang-long|Thang Long]], ruling from Hue over the whole of present-day [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] for the first time.
nguyen-dynasty.r: [[e:gia-long|Gia Long]] and [[e:minh-mang|Minh Mang]] built a centralised Confucian state modelled on the Qing, with a law code, examinations, citadels and the Hue imperial city. Minh Mang renamed the country Dai Nam in 1839, annexed [[e:champa|Champa's]] remnant and occupied [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]]. Persecution of Catholic missionaries gave [[e:france|France]] a pretext to intervene.
nguyen-dynasty.e: [[e:france|France]] seized [[s:french-cochinchina|Cochinchina]] from 1858 and imposed [[e:protectorate|protectorates]] over [[s:french-protectorate-of-annam|Annam]] and [[s:french-protectorate-of-tonkin|Tonkin]] in 1883 and 1884, leaving the emperors as figureheads. After the Japanese coup of March 1945 [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]] declared the [[s:empire-of-vietnam|Empire of Vietnam]], and in August 1945 he abdicated to the [[e:viet-minh|Viet Minh]].

najdiyya.t: A Kharijite state in central and eastern Arabia that briefly ruled al-Yamama, Bahrain and Oman during the civil war of the 680s.
najdiyya.o: The Najdiyya took their name from [[e:najda-ibn-amir-al-hanafi|Najda ibn Amir al-Hanafi]], a Kharijite leader who broke with the more extreme [[e:azariqa|Azariqa]]. During the [[e:second-fitna|Second Fitna]] he seized al-[[e:yamama|Yamama]], his tribe's [[e:bantustan|homeland]] in [[e:najd|Najd]], around 686 and was acknowledged as commander of the faithful by his followers.
najdiyya.r: [[e:najda-ibn-amir-al-hanafi|Najda]]'s forces conquered [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]], [[e:oman|Oman]] and parts of [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]] and [[s:kingdom-of-hadramawt|Hadramawt]] and threatened [[e:taif|Ta'if]], challenging the [[s:caliphate-of-ibn-al-zubayr|Caliphate of Ibn al-Zubayr]]. He was more moderate than other [[e:kharijites|Kharijites]], allowing those who did not join him to live unharmed and relying on reasoned judgement where the [[e:quran|Quran]] was silent. Internal disputes over the treatment of captives and payments to followers divided the movement.
najdiyya.e: Around 691 his own followers deposed and killed [[e:najda-ibn-amir-al-hanafi|Najda]] and turned to [[e:abu-fudayk|Abu Fudayk]]. After the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyads]] reunited the [[e:caliphate|caliphate]], an army sent by [[e:abd-al-malik-ibn-marwan|Abd al-Malik]] defeated Abu Fudayk in [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] in 693, ending the state.

nazi-germany.t: Hitler's totalitarian dictatorship, which launched the Second World War and carried out the Holocaust before its total defeat in 1945.
nazi-germany.o: [[e:adolf-hitler|Adolf Hitler]] was appointed chancellor on 30 January 1933. Using the [[e:reichstag-fire-decree|Reichstag Fire Decree]] of February 1933 and the [[e:enabling-act-of-1933|Enabling Act]] of March 1933, the Nazis abolished civil liberties, banned other parties, dissolved trade unions and subordinated the German states. On [[e:paul-von-hindenburg|Hindenburg]]'s death in 1934 Hitler combined the offices of chancellor and president as [[e:fuhrer|Führer]].
nazi-germany.r: The regime ruled through terror, propaganda and the SS and [[e:gestapo|Gestapo]], and persecuted [[e:jews|Jews]] through the [[e:nuremberg-laws|Nuremberg Laws]] of 1935 and the November pogrom of 1938. It rearmed, annexed [[e:austria|Austria]] and the [[e:sudetenland|Sudetenland]] in 1938 and invaded [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1939, starting the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]]. In occupied [[e:europe|Europe]] it murdered some six million Jews, as well as [[e:romani-people|Roma]], Soviet prisoners and others.
nazi-germany.e: Allied armies invaded [[e:germany|Germany]] from east and west, [[e:adolf-hitler|Hitler]] killed himself in [[e:berlin|Berlin]] on 30 April 1945, and the [[e:wehrmacht|Wehrmacht]] surrendered unconditionally on 8 May 1945. Germany was occupied and divided, and its leaders were tried at [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]].

niger-coast-protectorate.t: The British protectorate in south-eastern Nigeria from 1893 to 1900, whose forces sacked Benin City in 1897.
niger-coast-protectorate.o: In 1893 the [[s:oil-rivers-protectorate|Oil Rivers Protectorate]] was extended inland and renamed the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] Coast [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]], under the commissioner and consul-general [[e:claude-maxwell-macdonald|Claude MacDonald]], with headquarters at [[s:old-calabar|Old Calabar]]. It was governed by the Foreign Office rather than the [[e:colonial-office|Colonial Office]], and its officials began pushing into the hinterland of the [[e:niger-delta|Niger Delta]].
niger-coast-protectorate.r: The [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] built customs posts, courts and a constabulary, and used force against rulers who obstructed trade. In 1894 it defeated the Itsekiri trader [[e:nana-olomu|Nana Olomu]] at [[e:ebrohimi|Ebrohimi]]. Under [[e:ralph-moor|Ralph Moor]], commissioner from 1896, an expedition in 1897 avenged the killing of acting consul [[e:james-robert-phillips|James Phillips]] by sacking [[e:benin-city|Benin City]], ending the independence of the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]] and seizing the [[e:benin-bronzes|Benin Bronzes]].
niger-coast-protectorate.e: On 1 January 1900 the [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] was merged with the southern lands of the [[s:royal-niger-company-territories|Royal Niger Company]] to form the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]]. The [[e:benin-bronzes|Benin Bronzes]] taken in 1897 remain the subject of [[e:repatriation-of-cultural-property|restitution]] campaigns.

ngonde-kingdom.t: A small kingdom at the northern tip of Lake Malawi ruled by the Kyungu, a sacred king kept in ritual seclusion.
ngonde-kingdom.o: According to tradition, the Kyungu dynasty arrived from the north-east and established itself over the farming and fishing people of the [[e:karonga|Karonga]] plain by around 1600. The capital at Mbande hill became the ritual centre of the kingdom.
ngonde-kingdom.r: The Kyungu was a divine king whose health was linked to the land's fertility; he lived in seclusion, governed through a council of nobles (makambala) and, by tradition, was put to death if he fell seriously ill. Commoners grew bananas and [[e:millet|millet]], kept [[e:cattle|cattle]] and fished in the lake, and the kingdom traded [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and iron goods with neighbours.
ngonde-kingdom.e: In the 1880s the Swahili-Arab trader Mlozi set up fortified bases near [[e:karonga|Karonga]], and the Ngonde were caught in the Karonga war of 1887–89 between Mlozi and the [[e:african-lakes-company|African Lakes Company]]. In 1891 the area became part of the [[s:british-central-africa-protectorate|British Central Africa Protectorate]], later [[s:nyasaland|Nyasaland]]. The Kyungu remains a traditional ruler in [[e:malawi|Malawi]].

northern-fujiwara.t: A family of northern warlords who ruled northeastern Japan for a century from Hiraizumi, whose golden temples rivalled the splendours of Kyoto.
northern-fujiwara.o: [[e:fujiwara-no-kiyohira|Fujiwara no Kiyohira]], a survivor of the Former Nine Years' and Later Three Years' Wars in [[e:mutsu-province|Mutsu]], emerged as master of the north after the [[e:kiyohara-clan|Kiyohara]] family collapsed in 1087. He made [[e:hiraizumi|Hiraizumi]] his base, claiming descent from the court Fujiwara through his father.
northern-fujiwara.r: Three generations, [[e:fujiwara-no-kiyohira|Kiyohira]], [[e:fujiwara-no-motohira|Motohira]] and [[e:fujiwara-no-hidehira|Hidehira]], governed [[e:mutsu-province|Mutsu]] and Dewa as semi-independent lords while acknowledging the court in [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]]. Their wealth came from gold mines, horses and trade in [[e:fur-trade|furs]], eagle feathers and goods from the far north. They built [[e:chuson-ji|Chuson-ji]] with its gold-leafed [[e:konjikido|Konjikido]] hall of 1124 and [[e:motsu-ji|Motsu-ji]] with its Pure Land garden.
northern-fujiwara.e: [[e:fujiwara-no-hidehira|Hidehira]] sheltered the fugitive [[e:minamoto-no-yoshitsune|Minamoto no Yoshitsune]]. After his death his son [[e:fujiwara-no-yasuhira|Yasuhira]] killed Yoshitsune under pressure from [[e:minamoto-no-yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]] in 1189, but Yoritomo invaded anyway, and the family was destroyed. [[e:hiraizumi|Hiraizumi]] is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

nolamba-dynasty.t: A minor dynasty of the southern Deccan, claiming Pallava descent, that ruled Nolambavadi and built the temples of Hemavati.
nolamba-dynasty.o: The Nolambas, who called themselves Nolamba [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallavas]] and claimed descent from the Pallava dynasty, emerged in the 8th century in Nolambavadi, a region covering parts of modern [[e:chitradurga|Chitradurga]], [[e:tumkur|Tumkur]], [[e:kolar|Kolar]] and [[e:anantapur|Anantapur]]. Their main capital was [[e:hemavathi|Hemavati]], in [[e:andhra-pradesh|Andhra Pradesh]] near the [[e:karnataka|Karnataka]] border.
nolamba-dynasty.r: The Nolambas served as feudatories of larger powers, at different times the [[s:western-ganga-dynasty|Western Ganga dynasty]], the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]] and the [[s:pallava-dynasty|Pallavas]], and often shifted allegiance. Their inscriptions are in [[e:kannada|Kannada]]. They built Shaiva temples, notably the Doddeshvara temple at [[e:hemavathi|Hemavati]], known for finely carved black stone pillars and ceilings, some now in museums.
nolamba-dynasty.e: In the 10th century the Ganga king [[e:marasimha-ii|Marasimha II]] attacked them, and the [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] and the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Western Chalukya Empire]] later fought over Nolambavadi. The Nolambas survived as minor chiefs until the mid-11th century.

nakhichevan-khanate.t: A khanate on the middle Araxes ruled by the Kangarlu tribe, ceded by Persia to Russia in 1828 and the forerunner of today's Nakhchivan.
nakhichevan-khanate.o: After [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah's]] death in 1747, [[e:haydar-quli-khan|Haydar Quli Khan]] of the Turkic [[e:kangarlu|Kangarlu]] tribe declared himself khan of [[e:nakhchivan|Nakhichevan]], an old trading town on the road from [[e:tabriz|Tabriz]] to the [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]]. The khanate covered the valleys along the [[e:aras-river|Araxes]] between Erivan and [[e:karabakh|Karabakh]].
nakhichevan-khanate.r: The khans relied on their [[e:kangarlu|Kangarlu]] tribesmen and on Armenian and Muslim farmers growing grain, [[e:cotton|cotton]] and fruit with irrigation, while the town traded salt from nearby mines. Their small state was squeezed between the [[s:erivan-khanate|Erivan Khanate]], the [[s:karabakh-khanate|Karabakh Khanate]] and [[e:persia|Persia]]; [[e:agha-mohammad-khan-qajar|Agha Muhammad Khan Qajar]] had [[e:kalbali-khan|Kalbali Khan]] blinded for his resistance.
nakhichevan-khanate.e: In the [[e:russo-persian-war-1826-1828|Russo-Persian War]] of 1826-1828, [[e:ehsan-khan-kangarlu|Ehsan Khan Kangarlu]] went over to [[e:russia|Russia]], and the [[e:treaty-of-turkmenchay|Treaty of Turkmenchay]] in 1828 ceded the khanate to the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]], which joined it with Erivan in the [[e:armenian-oblast|Armenian Oblast]].

nagpur-kingdom.t: The Maratha kingdom of the Bhonsles of Nagpur, which raided Bengal, ruled Orissa and was annexed by the British under the doctrine of lapse.
nagpur-kingdom.o: [[e:raghuji-i-bhonsle|Raghuji Bhonsle]], a [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] general, was sent to [[e:berar|Berar]] and [[e:gondwana-india|Gondwana]] and around 1739 established himself at [[e:nagpur|Nagpur]], absorbing the [[e:gond-people|Gond]] kingdom of Deogarh. His armies invaded [[e:bengal|Bengal]] repeatedly in the 1740s, and in 1751 Nawab [[e:alivardi-khan|Alivardi Khan]] ceded [[e:odisha|Orissa]] to him.
nagpur-kingdom.r: The [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] were among the great [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] houses, often rivals of the [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]], and ruled a large but thinly populated realm of central [[e:india|India]]. [[e:raghuji-ii-bhonsle|Raghuji II]] was defeated with [[e:scindias|Scindia]] at [[e:battle-of-assaye|Assaye]] and [[e:battle-of-argaon|Argaon]] in 1803 and lost [[e:odisha|Orissa]] and western [[e:berar|Berar]] by the [[e:treaty-of-deogaon|Treaty of Deogaon]]. [[e:mudhoji-ii-bhonsle|Appa Sahib's]] attack on the British at [[e:battle-of-sitabuldi|Sitabuldi]] in 1817 led to the loss of more land and close British control.
nagpur-kingdom.e: When [[e:raghuji-iii-bhonsle|Raghuji III]] died without a son in 1853, [[e:lord-dalhousie|Lord Dalhousie]] annexed the kingdom under the doctrine of lapse. Its lands formed the [[e:nagpur-province|Nagpur Province]] and later the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces]].

northern-satraps.t: Saka governors who ruled Mathura around the turn of the era and left the famous Mathura Lion Capital.
northern-satraps.o: The Northern [[e:satrapy|Satraps]] were [[e:indo-scythians|Indo-Scythian]] governors who took control of [[e:mathura|Mathura]] on the [[e:yamuna|Yamuna]], probably in the 1st century BCE, as [[s:saka|Saka]] power spread from the north-west. Their best-known ruler, [[e:rajuvula|Rajuvula]], styled himself great satrap and issued coins copying [[e:indo-greek-kingdom|Indo-Greek]] designs.
northern-satraps.r: The [[e:satrapy|satraps]] ruled a city that was already a major religious centre. The [[e:mathura-lion-capital|Mathura Lion Capital]], inscribed in Kharoshthi, records gifts to the Buddhist community by [[e:rajuvula|Rajuvula's]] chief queen. His son [[e:sodasa|Sodasa]] issued inscriptions in Brahmi, including one recording a temple to Vasudeva, which shows the rulers supporting both [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] and early [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnavism]]. [[e:jainism|Jain]] communities also flourished in the city.
northern-satraps.e: Within a few decades the [[s:kushan-empire|Kushan Empire]] absorbed [[e:mathura|Mathura]], which became its southern capital and a major centre of sculpture. The satrapal system survived further south among the [[s:western-satraps|Western Satraps]].

new-netherland.t: The Dutch colony on the Hudson River, whose port of New Amsterdam became New York and whose tolerant, commercial character shaped the city.
new-netherland.o: [[e:henry-hudson|Henry Hudson]] explored the river named after him for the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] in 1609, and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] traders were soon buying [[e:fur-trade|furs]] there; the [[e:new-netherland-company|New Netherland Company]] built a post near modern [[e:albany-new-york|Albany]] in 1614. After 1621 the [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] of the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]] took over, and in 1626 [[e:peter-minuit|Peter Minuit]] bought [[e:manhattan|Manhattan]] from the [[e:lenape|Lenape]].
new-netherland.r: The company governed through a director-general and council, and the colony lived on the [[e:fur-trade|fur trade]] through [[e:fort-orange|Fort Orange]], with settlers drawn from many nations. [[e:patroon|Patroonships]] such as [[e:rensselaerswyck|Rensselaerswyck]] offered large estates to investors. [[e:willem-kieft|Willem Kieft's]] war with the [[e:lenape|Lenape]] in 1643 to 1645 nearly ruined the colony. [[e:peter-stuyvesant|Peter Stuyvesant]], governing from 1647, conquered [[s:new-sweden|New Sweden]] in 1655 and built the wall that gave Wall Street its name. Residents of [[e:flushing-queens|Flushing]] protested his intolerance in 1657.
new-netherland.e: In 1664 an English fleet seized [[e:new-amsterdam|New Amsterdam]] without a fight, and it became the [[s:province-of-new-york|Province of New York]], confirmed by the [[e:treaty-of-breda-1667|Treaty of Breda]] in 1667. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] briefly retook the colony in 1673 to 1674. Dutch place names and customs persisted in the [[e:hudson-valley|Hudson Valley]].

cr.a: Miyamaki, Oren neu dag, Artem Karimov, Golradir

north-peruvian-republic.t: The northern Peruvian state, ruled from Lima, that formed part of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation between 1836 and 1839.
north-peruvian-republic.o: Following the creation of the [[s:south-peruvian-republic|South Peruvian Republic]], an assembly of the northern [[e:departement|departments]], including [[e:lima|Lima]], [[e:la-libertad-region|La Libertad]] and [[e:junin-region|Junín]], met at Huaura in August 1836 and created the North Peruvian Republic. [[e:luis-jose-de-orbegoso|Luis José de Orbegoso]], who had invited [[e:andres-de-santa-cruz|Andrés de Santa Cruz]] into [[e:peru|Peru]], became its president.
north-peruvian-republic.r: The republic joined the [[s:peru-bolivian-confederation|Peru-Bolivian Confederation]] under [[e:andres-de-santa-cruz|Santa Cruz]] as Supreme Protector. Many [[e:lima|Lima]] elites resented what they saw as Bolivian domination and the division of [[e:peru|Peru]], and Peruvian exiles in [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] campaigned against it. In 1838, as a Chilean expedition advanced, [[e:luis-jose-de-orbegoso|Orbegoso]] broke with Santa Cruz and declared the North Peruvian Republic independent of the confederation, but was defeated by the Chileans outside Lima.
north-peruvian-republic.e: After the battle of [[e:battle-of-yungay|Yungay]] in January 1839 ended the confederation, [[e:agustin-gamarra|Agustín Gamarra]] restored a unified [[s:republic-of-peru|Republic of Peru]]. [[e:luis-jose-de-orbegoso|Orbegoso]] went into exile, and a constitution adopted at [[e:huancayo|Huancayo]] in 1839 strengthened central government. The episode deepened the rivalry between [[e:peru|Peru]] and [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]].

naxos.t: Largest island of the Cyclades, an Archaic marble-working power whose failed siege by Persia in 499 BCE set off the Ionian Revolt.
naxos.o: Naxos was settled by [[e:ionia|Ionian Greeks]] in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], building on a long Cycladic and Mycenaean past. Its fertile valleys and white marble made it the leading island of the [[e:cyclades|Cyclades]] by the 7th century BCE. Tradition linked it with [[e:dionysus|Dionysus]] and with [[e:ariadne|Ariadne]].
naxos.r: Naxian sculptors made colossal kouroi, the Naxian Sphinx at [[s:delphi|Delphi]] and the Lions on [[s:delos|Delos]]. The tyrant [[e:lygdamis-of-naxos|Lygdamis]], helped by [[e:peisistratus|Peisistratus]], ruled in the mid-6th century BCE, when the great unfinished temple gateway, the [[e:portara|Portara]], was begun. In 499 BCE [[e:aristagoras-of-miletus|Aristagoras of Miletus]] and the [[e:persians|Persians]] failed to capture Naxos, a fiasco that triggered the [[e:ionian-revolt|Ionian Revolt]].
naxos.e: [[e:persia|Persia]] sacked Naxos in 490 BCE. It was the first member to try to leave the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] and was subdued c. 470 BCE. Later it joined Hellenistic leagues and passed under [[e:rome|Rome]] by 146 BCE.

numayrids.t: Arab emirs of the Banu Numayr who ruled Harran and the towns of the western Jazira for nearly a century.
numayrids.o: The Banu Numayr were a [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] tribe of the [[e:banu-amir|Amir ibn Sa'sa'a]] who moved into the [[e:diyar-mudar|Diyar Mudar]], the region between the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] and the [[e:balikh-river|Balikh]]. Around 990, as [[e:hamdanid-dynasty|Hamdanid]] power faded, their chief [[e:waththab-ibn-sabiq|Waththab ibn Sabiq]] seized [[e:harran|Harran]], and the tribe went on to hold [[e:saruj|Saruj]], [[e:raqqa|Raqqa]] and for a time [[s:county-of-edessa|Edessa]].
numayrids.r: The Numayrids were tribal [[e:emir|emirs]] who lived partly as nomads and relied on the townspeople and on dues from the fertile river valleys. They balanced between the [[e:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimids]], the [[s:mirdasid-emirate|Mirdasids]] of [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]], the [[s:marwanids|Marwanids]] and [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]. [[e:harran|Harran]] still had a community of Sabian star-worshippers, whose temple the Numayrids are said to have turned into a palace. In 1031 they lost [[s:county-of-edessa|Edessa]] to Byzantine forces under [[e:george-maniakes|George Maniakes]].
numayrids.e: The [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuk]] advance weakened the [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] [[e:emirate|emirates]]. Around 1081 the [[e:uqaylid-dynasty|Uqaylid]] emir [[e:muslim-ibn-quraysh|Muslim ibn Quraysh]] took [[e:harran|Harran]], ending Numayrid rule; the tribe itself survived in the region.

nawabate-of-bengal.t: The hereditary regime of the Nawabs of Bengal at Murshidabad, whose defeat at Plassey in 1757 opened India to British rule.
nawabate-of-bengal.o: [[e:murshid-quli-khan|Murshid Quli Khan]], appointed [[e:diwan|diwan]] of [[e:bengal|Bengal]] by [[e:aurangzeb|Aurangzeb]], moved the revenue office to [[e:murshidabad|Murshidabad]] and in 1717 became governor (subahdar) as well. Under him and his successors Bengal, [[e:bihar|Bihar]] and [[e:odisha|Odisha]] became a largely autonomous hereditary state, nominally loyal to the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] but sending only fixed tribute.
nawabate-of-bengal.r: The nawabs relied on [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] bankers such as the [[e:jagat-seth|Jagat Seths]] and on zamindars for revenue. [[e:bengal|Bengal]] was the richest province of [[e:india|India]], exporting [[e:silk|silk]], muslin and saltpetre through European companies at [[e:kolkata|Calcutta]], [[e:chinsurah|Chinsurah]] and [[e:chandannagar|Chandernagore]]. [[e:alivardi-khan|Alivardi Khan]] fought [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] raids in the 1740s. [[e:siraj-ud-daulah|Siraj ud-Daulah]] attacked Calcutta in 1756.
nawabate-of-bengal.e: [[e:robert-clive|Robert Clive's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-plassey|Plassey]] in 1757, helped by [[e:mir-jafar|Mir Jafar's]] betrayal, made the nawabs dependent on the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]]. After the [[e:battle-of-buxar|Battle of Buxar]] the Company received the diwani in 1765, beginning [[s:company-rule-in-india|Company rule in India]]; the nawabs survived as pensioners.

natalia-republic.t: The Voortrekker republic in Natal, created after the victory at Blood River and annexed by Britain within five years.
natalia-republic.o: [[e:voortrekkers|Voortrekkers]] crossed the [[e:drakensberg|Drakensberg]] into [[s:natal-colony|Natal]] in 1837. After [[e:dingane|Dingane's]] men killed [[e:piet-retief|Piet Retief's]] party in 1838, [[e:andries-pretorius|Andries Pretorius]] led the commando that defeated the [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]] at [[e:battle-of-blood-river|Blood River]] in December 1838. The trekkers founded [[e:pietermaritzburg|Pietermaritzburg]] and organised a republic with a Volksraad in 1839.
natalia-republic.r: The [[e:volksraad|Volksraad]] held supreme power in a weak, quarrelsome government. In 1840 the [[e:boers|Boers]] helped [[e:mpande|Mpande]] overthrow [[e:dingane|Dingane]] and seized thousands of [[e:cattle|cattle]] from the [[s:zulu-kingdom|Zulu Kingdom]]. Farms were laid out across the uplands, and the Volksraad's plan to move Africans southwards alarmed the Cape government.
natalia-republic.e: British troops occupied [[e:durban|Port Natal]] in 1842; the [[e:boers|Boers]] won at [[e:battle-of-congella|Congella]] and besieged them, until [[e:dick-king|Dick King's]] ride to [[e:makhanda|Grahamstown]] brought relief. Natalia submitted, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed it in 1843 as the [[s:natal-colony|Natal Colony]], and many trekkers moved back over the [[e:drakensberg|Drakensberg]].

nagaoka-domain.t: A small Echigo domain whose leader Kawai Tsugunosuke fought one of the hardest battles of the Boshin War against the imperial army in 1868.
nagaoka-domain.o: The [[e:shogun|shogunate]] gave Nagaoka in [[e:echigo-province|Echigo]] to [[e:makino-tadanari|Makino Tadanari]] in 1618, with about 74,000 koku. His descendants ruled until the end of the period, and the domain's code of spartan [[e:samurai|samurai]] behaviour was proverbial.
nagaoka-domain.r: Nagaoka controlled the middle course of the [[e:shinano-province|Shinano]] river and the port of [[e:niigata|Niigata]] until the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] took it over in 1843. In the 1860s the senior retainer [[e:kawai-tsugunosuke|Kawai Tsugunosuke]] reformed finances and the army, buying modern rifles and [[e:gatling-gun|Gatling guns]], and sought armed neutrality between the shogunate and the new government.
nagaoka-domain.e: When the imperial army refused talks in 1868, Nagaoka joined the [[s:ouetsu-reppan-domei|Ouetsu Reppan Domei]]. Its castle fell, was retaken and fell again; Kawai died of wounds. In 1870 the retainer [[e:kobayashi-torasaburo|Kobayashi Torasaburo]] used a gift of a hundred sacks of [[e:rice|rice]] to found a school, a story later famous. It became part of [[e:niigata-prefecture|Niigata Prefecture]].

navajo-nation.t: The largest Native American reservation and self-governing nation in the United States, founded on the treaty of 1868 that ended the Navajo exile.
navajo-nation.o: In 1863 and 1864 the US Army under [[e:kit-carson|Kit Carson]] waged a scorched-earth campaign against the [[e:navajo|Diné]], then forced about 9,000 of them on the [[e:long-walk-of-the-navajo|Long Walk]] to [[e:bosque-redondo|Bosque Redondo]] in [[e:new-mexico|New Mexico]], where many died. The Treaty of 1868, signed on 1 June, allowed the Navajo to return to a reservation within their [[e:bantustan|homeland]] between four sacred mountains.
navajo-nation.r: The reservation was repeatedly enlarged and now covers about 70,000 square kilometres in [[e:arizona|Arizona]], [[e:new-mexico|New Mexico]] and [[e:utah|Utah]]. A tribal council was created in 1923, chiefly to approve oil leases, with [[e:henry-chee-dodge|Henry Chee Dodge]] as chairman, and Window Rock became the capital in the 1930s. The federal livestock reduction of the 1930s devastated herding families. [[e:navajo-code-talkers|Navajo Code Talkers]] served the [[e:united-states-marine-corps|Marines]] in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]].
navajo-nation.e: The tribe adopted the name [[e:navajo|Navajo]] Nation in 1969 and reorganised its government into three branches from 1989. It continues as a sovereign nation within the [[s:united-states|United States]], contending with poverty and the legacy of uranium mining while maintaining one of the most widely spoken Native languages.
navajo-nation.re: Navajo religion, Native American Church, Christianity

northern-ireland.t: The part of the United Kingdom in north-east Ireland, created by partition in 1921 and marked by decades of conflict and a power-sharing peace.
northern-ireland.o: The [[e:government-of-ireland-act-1920|Government of Ireland Act 1920]] created Northern Ireland from six of Ulster's nine counties, where Protestants, mostly unionists, were a majority. Its Parliament opened in June 1921, and it opted out of the [[s:irish-free-state|Irish Free State]] in December 1922.
northern-ireland.r: Northern Ireland was governed for fifty years by the [[e:ulster-unionist-party|Ulster Unionist Party]] from [[e:stormont|Stormont]], with discrimination against the Catholic, mainly nationalist minority. [[e:belfast|Belfast]] was a centre of shipbuilding and linen. The civil rights movement of the late 1960s was followed by the [[e:the-troubles|Troubles]], which killed about 3,600 people, and direct rule from [[e:london|London]] from 1972.
northern-ireland.e: The [[e:good-friday-agreement|Good Friday Agreement]] of 1998 established a power-sharing Assembly and Executive and confirmed that Northern Ireland remains in the [[s:united-kingdom|United Kingdom]] unless its people vote otherwise.
