nagnatae.t: People of north-west Ireland recorded by Ptolemy, who also names a notable town of theirs called Nagnata.
nagnatae.o: [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 places the Nagnatae on the north-west coast of Ireland, roughly in [[e:county-sligo|Sligo]] or north [[e:county-mayo|Mayo]], and lists a settlement called Nagnata, which he describes as a notable town. His information came from earlier sailors' reports on the Atlantic coast.
nagnatae.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers, economy or customs. The identification of Nagnata is disputed; sites around [[e:sligo-bay|Sligo Bay]] have been suggested, and some versions of the text spell the people Magnatae, which has led to other proposed meanings. The region was rich in older monuments such as the [[e:carrowmore|Carrowmore]] tombs.
nagnatae.e: No later source mentions the Nagnatae. Their area later lay within the [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Kingdom of Connacht]], ruled by branches of the [[e:connachta|Connachta]] dynasties.

nosy-be.t: An island off northwest Madagascar placed under French protection in 1841, an early base for France's later conquest of Madagascar.
nosy-be.o: [[e:sakalava|Sakalava]] rulers of [[s:boina|Boina]], retreating before the [[s:merina-kingdom|Merina Kingdom]], took refuge on Nosy Be and neighbouring islands. Their queen, [[e:tsiomeko|Tsiomeko]], sought French protection, and in 1841 the island was ceded to [[e:france|France]] through Admiral de Hell, governor of [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]], after whom its main town, [[e:hell-ville|Hell-Ville]], was named.
nosy-be.r: French administrators developed [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] cane plantations, using Malagasy, Comoran and later contract labourers, and the island became a trading centre for northwest [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]]. It was governed as a small dependency, at times jointly with [[s:colony-of-mayotte-and-dependencies|Mayotte]], and offered [[e:france|France]] a strategic claim to the Malagasy coast.
nosy-be.e: After the conquest of [[e:madagascar|Madagascar]], Nosy Be was merged in 1896 into the new colony of [[s:french-madagascar|French Madagascar]]. It later became known for ylang-ylang essential oil, vanilla and tourism.

nagar-state.t: A mountain principality of the Karakoram, facing Hunza across the gorge of the Hunza river, ruled by Shia Mirs until Pakistan abolished it in 1974.
nagar-state.o: The Mirs of [[s:nagar|Nagar]] belonged to the Maglot dynasty, which according to local tradition shared its ancestry with the rulers of [[s:hunza-state|Hunza]], two brothers having divided the valley. The register's start date is approximate; the principality's early history rests on oral tradition.
nagar-state.r: Nagar's people, mostly [[e:burushaski|Burushaski]] and [[e:shina-language|Shina]] speakers, are [[e:twelver-shiism|Twelver]] Shia Muslims. The state lived from irrigated terraces and herding in the high valleys below [[e:rakaposhi|Rakaposhi]]. Long rivalry with [[s:hunza-state|Hunza]] alternated with alliance. In 1891 British forces stormed the fort of Nilt in the [[e:hunza-nagar-campaign|Hunza-Nagar campaign]], after which [[s:nagar|Nagar]] became a dependency under the [[e:gilgit-agency|Gilgit Agency]] and the suzerainty of [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir]].
nagar-state.e: The Mir acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in 1947. [[s:nagar|Nagar]] remained a self-governing principality until [[e:zulfikar-ali-bhutto|Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's]] government abolished it in 1974, and it is now a district of [[e:gilgit-baltistan|Gilgit-Baltistan]].

ngo-dynasty.t: The first independent Vietnamese dynasty after a thousand years of Chinese rule, founded by Ngo Quyen after his victory at Bach Dang in 938.
ngo-dynasty.o: In 938 [[e:ngo-quyen|Ngo Quyen]], son-in-law of [[e:duong-dinh-nghe|Duong Dinh Nghe]], defeated the [[s:southern-han|Southern Han]] navy on the [[e:bach-dang-river|Bach Dang]] river by planting iron-tipped stakes in the riverbed and luring the fleet onto them at low tide. In 939 he declared himself king and set his capital at [[e:co-loa-citadel|Co Loa]], the ancient citadel of [[s:au-lac|Au Lac]].
ngo-dynasty.r: [[e:ngo-quyen|Ngo Quyen]] established a court with officials and rituals on the Chinese model, but his authority depended on alliances with regional strongmen. After his death in 944 his brother-in-law [[e:duong-tam-kha|Duong Tam Kha]] seized power, until Ngo Quyen's sons [[e:ngo-xuong-ngap|Ngo Xuong Ngap]] and [[e:ngo-xuong-van|Ngo Xuong Van]] restored the family and ruled jointly.
ngo-dynasty.e: The dynasty lost control as local warlords asserted themselves, and after [[e:ngo-xuong-van|Ngo Xuong Van's]] death in 965 the country broke into the period of the Twelve Warlords. [[e:dinh-tien-hoang|Dinh Bo Linh]] reunified it in 968, founding the [[s:dinh-dynasty|Dinh dynasty]]. [[e:bach-dang-river|Bach Dang]] became a national symbol of resistance.

nazca.t: A culture of Peru's southern desert famed for the Nazca Lines, giant figures and lines drawn on the desert floor, and for its brightly painted pottery.
nazca.o: The Nazca culture grew out of the late [[s:paracas|Paracas]] tradition around 100 BCE in the Río Grande de Nazca and [[e:ica-river|Ica]] valleys of southern [[e:peru|Peru]]. In its early phase the adobe ceremonial centre of Cahuachi, with dozens of mounds, served as a pilgrimage site for scattered farming communities.
nazca.r: Nazca appears to have been a group of chiefdoms linked by shared ritual rather than a centralised state. Its people created the [[e:nazca-lines|Nazca Lines]], hundreds of straight lines and figures of a monkey, hummingbird and spider scraped into the pampa, likely connected to water and fertility rites. They built underground [[e:aqueduct|aqueducts]] called puquios to tap [[e:groundwater-depletion|groundwater]]. Their polychrome pottery used up to a dozen slip colours, and trophy heads feature prominently in their art.
nazca.e: Cahuachi lost importance by about 400 CE, and late Nazca society suffered from droughts and conflict. From around 650 CE the region came under the influence of the [[s:wari-empire|Wari Empire]], and the Nazca style faded. The Lines became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1994.

new-kingdom-of-granada.t: The Spanish colony created in Colombia's Andean highlands after the conquest of the Muisca, ruled from Santa Fe de Bogotá and the forerunner of Colombia.
new-kingdom-of-granada.o: [[e:gonzalo-jimenez-de-quesada|Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada]] led an expedition up the [[e:magdalena-river|Magdalena]] river and conquered the [[s:muisca-confederation|Muisca]] between 1537 and 1539. He founded [[e:bogota|Santa Fe de Bogotá]] in 1538 and named the land the [[e:new-kingdom-of-egypt|New Kingdom]] of [[e:granada|Granada]] after his home region in [[e:spain|Spain]]. In 1549 a [[e:audiencia|Royal Audiencia]] was established at Santa Fe.
new-kingdom-of-granada.r: From 1564 the territory was governed by a president of the [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] within the [[s:viceroyalty-of-peru|Viceroyalty of Peru]]. Its economy depended on gold from [[e:antioquia-department|Antioquia]], [[e:popayan|Popayán]] and the [[e:choco-department|Chocó]], mined increasingly by enslaved Africans, as well as emeralds from [[e:muzo|Muzo]]. [[e:cartagena-colombia|Cartagena de Indias]] was the main port and a centre of the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]]. The indigenous population fell sharply and was subject to [[e:encomienda|encomienda]] and forced labour. The [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] [[e:peter-claver|Peter Claver]] ministered to enslaved Africans in Cartagena.
new-kingdom-of-granada.e: In 1717 the Spanish crown elevated the [[e:new-kingdom-of-egypt|New Kingdom]] of [[e:granada|Granada]] into the [[s:viceroyalty-of-new-granada|Viceroyalty of New Granada]], separating it from [[e:peru|Peru]] and adding [[e:quito|Quito]], [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]] and [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]]. Its name survived in the [[s:republic-of-new-granada|Republic of New Granada]] after independence, and [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] remains the capital of [[s:republic-of-colombia|Colombia]].

najahid-dynasty.t: A dynasty of Ethiopian former slaves who ruled Zabid and the Yemeni Tihama for over a century amid wars with the Sulayhids.
najahid-dynasty.o: Najah was an Ethiopian slave commander serving the last rulers of the [[s:ziyadid-dynasty|Ziyadid dynasty]] at [[e:zabid|Zabid]]. Around 1022 he took power for himself, gained recognition from the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid]] [[e:caliphate|caliph]] and founded a dynasty that ruled the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] coastal plain of [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]].
najahid-dynasty.r: The Najahids governed through Ethiopian slave troops and ministers, a pattern inherited from the [[s:ziyadid-dynasty|Ziyadids]], and supported [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] scholarship in [[e:zabid|Zabid]]. Their history was dominated by war with the [[e:ismailism|Isma'ili]] [[s:sulayhid-dynasty|Sulayhid dynasty]] of the highlands: Najah was poisoned around 1060, and his son [[e:said-al-ahwal|Sa'id al-Ahwal]] later killed the Sulayhid ruler [[e:ali-ibn-muhammad-al-sulayhi|Ali ibn Muhammad]]. Zabid changed hands several times, and in the 12th century [[e:vizier|viziers]] held real power.
najahid-dynasty.e: Weakened by internal rivalries, the dynasty fell to the [[s:mahdid-dynasty|Mahdid dynasty]] of [[e:ali-ibn-mahdi|Ali ibn Mahdi]], who captured [[e:zabid|Zabid]] in 1159 after years of raids. The Ethiopian elite was largely destroyed.

narsinghpur-state.t: A small princely state on the Mahanadi in central Odisha, one of the Orissa Tributary States ruled by local Rajas until 1948.
narsinghpur-state.o: Tradition places the foundation of the ruling family in the late 13th century, but its early history is not well recorded.
narsinghpur-state.r: Narsinghpur was a small agricultural and forested state on the north bank of the [[e:mahanadi|Mahanadi]], west of [[e:cuttack|Cuttack]]. It paid tribute to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] in the 18th century and from 1803 was one of the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]] under British supervision.
narsinghpur-state.e: Narsinghpur merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now part of [[e:cuttack|Cuttack]] district.

negara-daha.t: The last Hindu kingdom of South Kalimantan, whose succession dispute gave rise to the Banjar Sultanate in 1526.
negara-daha.o: According to the [[e:hikayat-banjar|Hikayat Banjar]], the royal seat of [[s:negara-dipa|Negara Dipa]] was moved downriver to a place called Negara, on the Negara River, and the kingdom became known as Negara Daha. The details come only from this later chronicle, and the dates are approximate.
negara-daha.r: Negara Daha controlled trade on the [[e:barito-river|Barito]] river system, and its rulers looked to Javanese models of kingship. Its port at Muara Bahan traded with [[e:java|Java]]. The chronicle names [[e:maharaja-sukarama|Maharaja Sukarama]] as king.
negara-daha.e: After [[e:maharaja-sukarama|Sukarama]]'s death his son [[e:pangeran-tumenggung|Pangeran Tumenggung]] seized the throne, and the king's grandson [[e:sultan-suriansyah|Raden Samudra]] fled to the coast. With military help from [[s:demak-sultanate|Demak]], Raden Samudra won the war, accepted [[e:islam|Islam]] and became [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Suriansyah, founding the [[s:banjar-sultanate|Banjar Sultanate]] in 1526. Pangeran Tumenggung submitted, and Negara Daha came to an end.

nairi.t: Nairi, a loose confederation of highland chiefdoms around Lake Van that fought Assyria and became the seedbed of Urartu.
nairi.o: Nairi was the Assyrian name for the mountain lands north of the [[e:tigris|Tigris]] around [[e:lake-van|Lake Van]]. After the [[e:late-bronze-age-collapse|Late Bronze Age collapse]], local chiefdoms of the region formed temporary coalitions to resist Assyrian raids, first recorded by [[e:tiglath-pileser-i|Tiglath-Pileser I]] c. 1100 BCE.
nairi.r: [[e:tiglath-pileser-i|Tiglath-Pileser I]] claimed to have defeated 23 kings of Nairi and set up an inscription near [[e:malazgirt|Malazgirt]]. Nairi had no capital; it was a patchwork of fortified villages living from herding, farming and metalworking, which paid tribute in horses and [[e:cattle|cattle]].
nairi.e: Repeated Assyrian campaigns under [[e:ashurnasirpal-ii|Ashurnasirpal II]] and [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] pushed the Nairi chiefdoms to unite. By the mid-9th century BCE most were absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-urartu|Kingdom of Urartu]].

narsinghgarh-state.t: An Umat Parmar Rajput state of Malwa, split from Rajgarh in 1681 and ruled from its lake-side capital.
narsinghgarh-state.o: Narsinghgarh was formed in 1681 when [[e:paras-ram|Paras Ram]], a member of the Umat Parmar ruling house of [[s:rajgarh-state|Rajgarh]], separated part of the family lands. The capital, Narsinghgarh, was built beside a lake among the hills.
narsinghgarh-state.r: The Rajas ruled a plateau territory of wheat and opium farmers. In the 18th century they paid tribute to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]], and under British paramountcy after 1818 the state was an eleven-gun salute state in the [[e:bhopal-agency|Bhopal Agency]].
narsinghgarh-state.e: Narsinghgarh joined [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948 and [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. The town lies in [[s:rajgarh-state|Rajgarh]] district.

nembe-kingdom.t: Ijaw kingdom on the Brass river, remembered for its 1895 raid on the Royal Niger Company's base at Akassa.
nembe-kingdom.o: Nembe was founded by [[e:ijaw-people|Ijaw]] communities in the swamps of the central-eastern [[e:niger-river|Niger]] delta, traditionally by the 15th century. Its position near the Brass river mouth gave access to the sea and the Niger's channels, and Europeans called the state Brass after its outlet.
nembe-kingdom.r: The [[e:amanyanabo|Amanyanabo]] ruled with the heads of trading houses, in a system similar to other delta states. Nembe traders bought slaves and later [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] from inland markets and sold them to European ships. In the 19th century Christian missions arrived, and the kingdom split into rival towns over religion and trade.
nembe-kingdom.e: Nembe signed a British treaty in 1884 and became part of the [[s:oil-rivers-protectorate|Oil Rivers Protectorate]]. When the [[s:royal-niger-company-territories|Royal Niger Company]] shut Nembe traders out of the [[e:niger-river|Niger]] markets, King [[e:frederick-william-koko|Frederick William Koko]] led an attack on [[e:akassa-raid|Akassa]] in 1895, and British forces burned Nembe in reprisal. The [[e:amanyanabo|Amanyanabo]] still reigns.

nesiotic-league.t: League of the Cycladic islands centred on Delos, created by Antigonus I and used by Hellenistic kings to control the Aegean.
nesiotic-league.o: Around 314 BCE [[e:antigonus-i-monophthalmus|Antigonus I Monophthalmus]], seeking support in the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] against rival successors of Alexander, organised the islands of the [[e:cyclades|Cyclades]] into a league with its headquarters at the sanctuary of [[e:apollo|Apollo]] on [[s:delos|Delos]]. Members celebrated festivals named after Antigonus and his son Demetrius.
nesiotic-league.r: Delegates of the islands met in a federal council (synedrion) on [[s:delos|Delos]], voted honours for royal patrons and handled common affairs, but real power lay with the protecting king. After the collapse of Demetrius, the league passed under Ptolemaic control in the 280s BCE; officials called nesiarchs and [[e:philocles-king-of-sidon|Philocles, king of Sidon]], acted for [[e:ptolemy-ii-philadelphus|Ptolemy II]], and the islanders founded the Ptolemaia festival.
nesiotic-league.e: Ptolemaic power in the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] waned in the mid-3rd century BCE and the league faded. It was revived around 200 BCE under Rhodian leadership, but ended in 167 BCE when [[e:rome|Rome]] gave [[s:delos|Delos]] to [[s:athens|Athens]] and declared it a free port, ending Rhodian dominance.

northern-qi.t: The Gao family's dynasty in north-eastern China, rich and cultured but famously unstable, whose law code and Buddhist art shaped the Sui and Tang.
northern-qi.o: The general [[e:gao-huan|Gao Huan]] had dominated [[s:eastern-wei|Eastern Wei]] from behind a puppet emperor since 534. In 550 his son [[e:emperor-wenxuan-of-northern-qi|Gao Yang]] deposed the last Eastern Wei ruler and proclaimed himself emperor of Qi at Ye, inheriting the wealthy and populous plains of [[e:hebei|Hebei]], [[e:henan|Henan]] and [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]], with a second power centre at [[e:jinyang|Jinyang]].
northern-qi.r: The court mixed a [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] military elite with [[e:han-chinese|Han Chinese]] [[e:scholar-officials|scholar-officials]], and rivalry between the two groups ran through its politics. Several emperors, [[e:emperor-wenxuan-of-northern-qi|Gao Yang]] above all, were notorious for cruelty and drunkenness, and palace purges were frequent. Yet the state was prosperous: its Code of 564 became a model for [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] and [[s:later-tang|Tang]] law, and [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] flourished, as the cave temples of [[e:xiangtangshan-caves|Xiangtangshan]] and the sculpture of [[e:qingzhou|Qingzhou]] show.
northern-qi.e: Under the last effective ruler, [[e:gao-wei|Gao Wei]], misrule and the execution of able generals such as [[e:hulu-guang|Hulü Guang]] weakened the army. [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]] of [[s:northern-zhou|Northern Zhou]] invaded in 576 and took Ye in 577, reuniting northern [[e:china|China]], a step towards the [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] reunification of 589.

new-republic-brazil.t: Brazil's current democratic era, founded in 1985 after military rule, with a citizens' constitution, the Real Plan and fiercely contested politics.
new-republic-brazil.o: The end of the [[s:brazilian-military-dictatorship|Brazilian military dictatorship]] came when an electoral college chose [[e:tancredo-neves|Tancredo Neves]] as president in January 1985. Neves fell ill and died before taking office, and his vice-president, [[e:jose-sarney|José Sarney]], became the first civilian president in 21 years.
new-republic-brazil.r: The Citizen Constitution of 1988 guaranteed broad rights and direct elections. [[e:fernando-collor-de-mello|Fernando Collor]], the first directly elected president, resigned during impeachment in 1992. [[e:fernando-henrique-cardoso|Fernando Henrique Cardoso's]] [[e:real-plan|Real Plan]] of 1994 ended hyperinflation. [[e:luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva|Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]], president from 2003 to 2010, expanded social programmes such as [[e:bolsa-familia|Bolsa Família]]. His successor [[e:dilma-rousseff|Dilma Rousseff]] was impeached in 2016 amid recession and the [[e:operation-car-wash|Car Wash]] corruption investigation.
new-republic-brazil.e: [[e:jair-bolsonaro|Jair Bolsonaro]] governed from 2019 to 2022 and lost to [[e:luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva|Lula]]; Bolsonaro's supporters stormed government buildings in [[e:brasilia|Brasília]] on 8 January 2023. In 2025 the Supreme Court convicted Bolsonaro of plotting a coup. [[e:brazil|Brazil]] remains [[e:latin-america|Latin America's]] largest democracy.

nayagarh-state.t: A princely state in the hills south-west of Cuttack in Odisha, ruled by a family of Rajput descent until 1948.
nayagarh-state.o: Tradition holds that the ruling family descended from a [[e:baghel|Baghel]] [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] who came from Rewa and founded the state around 1500. Its early history is not well recorded.
nayagarh-state.r: Nayagarh was an agricultural state of valleys and wooded hills. It was tributary to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and, from 1803, one of the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary Mahals]] under British supervision. Little detailed history survives.
nayagarh-state.e: Nayagarh merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and is now the headquarters of Nayagarh district.

nippur.t: The holy city of Enlil, chief god of the Sumerians, whose temple granted legitimacy to any king who claimed to rule Sumer and Akkad.
nippur.o: Nippur was inhabited from the [[e:ubaid-period|Ubaid period]] and by the [[e:early-dynastic-period|Early Dynastic period]] had become the religious heart of [[e:sumer|Sumer]]. Lying between north and south, it never produced a dynasty in the [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]]; instead rulers of [[s:kish|Kish]], [[s:uruk|Uruk]], Ur and [[s:lagash|Lagash]] competed for control of it and recorded gifts to its temple, the [[e:ekur|E-kur]].
nippur.r: Nippur was governed by temple officials and local governors, and its authority was religious rather than military: recognition by [[e:enlil|Enlil]] at Nippur confirmed a ruler as overlord of the land. The city was also a centre of learning. Thousands of school tablets from the early second millennium BCE preserve much of the surviving Sumerian literature, including hymns, laments and the [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]] itself.
nippur.e: Its independence, such as it was, ended when [[e:sargon-of-akkad|Sargon of Akkad]] conquered [[e:sumer|Sumer]] around 2334 BCE. Nippur nevertheless remained a major cult and scribal city under later empires, including the Kassite and Persian periods, when the [[e:murashu-archive|Murashu]] business archive was written, and it was occupied until around 800 CE.

new-hebrides-condominium.t: A unique joint colony ruled by both Britain and France for 74 years, with two governments, two police forces and two legal systems, which became Vanuatu.
new-hebrides-condominium.o: French and British settlers, planters and missionaries competed in the New [[e:hebrides|Hebrides]] from the mid-19th century, and neither power would let the other annex the islands. After a joint naval commission was set up in 1887, an Anglo-French convention of 1906 created a condominium, refined by a protocol of 1914.
new-hebrides-condominium.r: Each power ran its own administration, police, schools, currency and courts for its own nationals, while a Joint Court, originally presided over by a judge appointed by the King of [[e:spain|Spain]], handled land and mixed cases. Ni-[[e:vanuatu|Vanuatu]] had no citizenship. Plantations produced copra and cocoa. During the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]] [[e:espiritu-santo|Espiritu Santo]] became a huge American base, and the [[e:john-frum-movement|John Frum movement]] spread on [[e:tanna|Tanna]].
new-hebrides-condominium.e: The [[e:vanuaaku-pati|Vanuaʻaku Pati]] under [[e:walter-lini|Walter Lini]] led the drive for independence, opposed by the [[e:nagriamel|Nagriamel]] movement of [[e:jimmy-stevens|Jimmy Stevens]], which attempted secession on [[e:espiritu-santo|Espiritu Santo]] in 1980. The New [[e:hebrides|Hebrides]] became independent as [[e:vanuatu|Vanuatu]] on 30 July 1980.
new-hebrides-condominium.re: Presbyterianism, Roman Catholicism, Anglicanism, Indigenous religions

numidia.t: The united Berber kingdom of Masinissa and Jugurtha, Rome's powerful ally and then enemy in North Africa.
numidia.o: After [[e:rome|Rome's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-zama|Zama]] in 202 BCE, [[e:masinissa|Masinissa]], king of the [[s:massylii|Massylii]], received the lands of the [[s:masaesyli|Masaesyli]] and united eastern and western Numidia into a single kingdom with its capital at [[e:cirta|Cirta]] (Constantine). Over fifty years he expanded at [[e:carthage|Carthage's]] expense.
numidia.r: [[e:masinissa|Masinissa]] encouraged settled farming, especially grain, and built a court that blended [[e:berbers|Berber]], Punic and Hellenistic culture; Punic was the language of administration. Royal tombs such as the [[e:medracen|Medracen]] show these mixed traditions. After his son [[e:micipsa|Micipsa]], the kingdom was divided among [[e:adherbal|Adherbal]], [[e:hiempsal-i|Hiempsal]] and [[e:jugurtha|Jugurtha]]. Jugurtha's killing of Italian traders at [[e:cirta|Cirta]] in 112 BCE led to the [[e:jugurthine-war|Jugurthine War]] with the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]].
numidia.e: [[e:jugurtha|Jugurtha]] was betrayed by [[e:bocchus-i|Bocchus I]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-mauretania|Kingdom of Mauretania]] and executed in [[e:rome|Rome]] in 104 BCE. Numidia survived as a client state until [[e:juba-i|Juba I]] backed [[e:pompey|Pompey's]] side and was defeated by [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] at [[e:battle-of-thapsus|Thapsus]] in 46 BCE. His kingdom became the province of [[e:africa-nova|Africa Nova]].

cr.a: Masinissa (0238?-0148 av. J.-C. ; roi de Numidie). Autorité émettrice de monnaie présumée Micipsa. Autorité émettrice...

nabataean-kingdom.t: The Nabataean Kingdom, an Arab trading state that controlled the incense routes and carved its capital Petra out of rose-red rock.
nabataean-kingdom.o: The Nabataeans were Arab nomads who controlled desert routes from southern [[e:arabia|Arabia]] to the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]]. By the 4th century BCE they were rich traders, and by 168 BCE they had a king, [[e:aretas-i|Aretas I]], who appears in the [[e:books-of-maccabees|Books of Maccabees]]. [[e:petra|Petra]], in the mountains of [[s:edom|Edom]], became their capital.
nabataean-kingdom.r: Nabataean kings ruled through control of the frankincense and [[e:myrrh|myrrh]] trade, protected caravans and built cisterns and channels to store desert water. [[e:petra|Petra's]] facades, such as [[e:al-khazneh|Al-Khazneh]], mix Greek, Egyptian and local styles. [[e:aretas-iii|Aretas III]] held [[e:damascus|Damascus]], and the Nabataean script developed into the Arabic alphabet.
nabataean-kingdom.e: The kingdom became a Roman client and declined as sea trade grew. When King [[e:rabbel-ii|Rabbel II]] died, [[e:trajan|Trajan]] annexed it in 106 CE as the province of [[e:arabia-petraea|Arabia Petraea]].

negara-dipa.t: A Hindu kingdom of South Kalimantan centred at Amuntai, remembered in the Hikayat Banjar as the first royal seat of the Banjar people.
negara-dipa.o: Negara Dipa is known chiefly from the [[e:hikayat-banjar|Hikayat Banjar]], the chronicle of the later Banjar court. It tells how a merchant from Keling named Ampu Jatmika settled on the Tabalong and Balangan rivers near modern [[e:amuntai|Amuntai]] and built a temple and palace. The register's dates of 1387 to 1495 are approximate.
negara-dipa.r: The chronicle says the founder did not claim kingship himself, and his son Lambung Mangkurat found a princess, Putri Junjung Buih, to marry a Javanese prince, so that the dynasty drew legitimacy from [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]]. The remains of the [[e:candi-agung|Candi Agung]] temple at [[e:amuntai|Amuntai]] are associated with this period. The kingdom traded gold, rattan and forest products down the [[e:barito-river|Barito]].
negara-dipa.e: According to the [[e:hikayat-banjar|Hikayat Banjar]], the royal seat later moved downriver and the kingdom became [[s:negara-daha|Negara Daha]]. Negara Daha in turn was replaced in 1526 by the [[s:banjar-sultanate|Banjar Sultanate]], which inherited its traditions.

north-caucasian-soviet-republic.t: A short-lived Soviet republic of 1918 uniting the Kuban, Black Sea, Terek and Stavropol soviets against the White armies.
north-caucasian-soviet-republic.o: In July 1918 the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Bolsheviks]] merged the [[s:kuban-black-sea-soviet-republic|Kuban-Black Sea Soviet Republic]] with the [[s:terek-soviet-republic|Terek Soviet Republic]] and the [[s:stavropol-soviet-republic|Stavropol Soviet Republic]], creating the North Caucasian Soviet Republic as part of the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]]. Its first capital was [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]]. The merger was meant to unite Red forces in the south against the advancing White armies and hostile [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]].
north-caucasian-soviet-republic.r: The republic was governed by a central executive committee and fought the [[e:volunteer-army|Volunteer Army]] of [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]], which took [[e:krasnodar|Yekaterinodar]] in August 1918 and forced the government to move to [[e:pyatigorsk|Pyatigorsk]]. Its large [[e:red-army|Red Army]] forces suffered from poor discipline and quarrels between party leaders and commanders, culminating in the commander [[e:ivan-sorokin|Ivan Sorokin's]] arrest and execution of the republic's leaders in October 1918.
north-caucasian-soviet-republic.e: [[e:ivan-sorokin|Sorokin]] was himself killed, and by the end of 1918 the [[e:white-movement|Whites]] had crushed the republic's army; it was abolished in December 1918. Its remnants retreated towards [[e:astrakhan|Astrakhan]], and Soviet rule returned to the [[e:north-caucasus|North Caucasus]] only in 1920.

ndwandwe-kingdom.t: The powerful kingdom of Zwide, chief rival of the early Zulu, whose defeat scattered leaders who founded new states across southern Africa.
ndwandwe-kingdom.o: The [[e:ndwandwe|Ndwandwe]] were settled around the [[e:mkuze-river|Mkhuze]] and [[e:pongola-river|Pongola]] rivers in the north of present-day [[e:kwazulu-natal|KwaZulu-Natal]], with ties to the Dlamini of the [[s:swazi-kingdom|Swazi Kingdom]]. Under Langa and especially his son [[e:zwide|Zwide]] in the late 18th and early 19th centuries, they expanded through conquest into a major power.
ndwandwe-kingdom.r: [[e:zwide|Zwide]] organised regiments and dominated his neighbours, driving [[e:sobhuza-i|Sobhuza I's]] people north and killing [[e:dingiswayo|Dingiswayo]] of the [[s:mthethwa-paramountcy|Mthethwa Paramountcy]] around 1818. His mother Ntombazi was a powerful figure at court. The struggle with [[e:shaka-zulu-king|Shaka]] produced battles such as [[e:battle-of-gqokli-hill|Gqokli Hill]] and the decisive [[e:ndwandwe|Ndwandwe]] defeat on the [[e:mhlatuze-river|Mhlatuze]] river around 1819.
ndwandwe-kingdom.e: [[e:zwide|Zwide]] moved north and died around 1825; his son Sikhunyana was defeated by [[e:shaka-zulu-king|Shaka]] in 1826. [[e:ndwandwe|Ndwandwe]] commanders [[e:soshangane|Soshangane]] and [[e:zwangendaba|Zwangendaba]] founded the [[s:gaza|Gaza]] state and the [[e:ngoni|Ngoni]] kingdoms far to the north.

north-eastern-rhodesia.t: The British South Africa Company's territory between the Luangwa valley and Lakes Tanganyika and Mweru, centred on Fort Jameson.
north-eastern-rhodesia.o: Company agents and British officials extended control over the lands east of the [[e:kafue-river|Kafue]] in the 1890s, defeating [[s:mpezenis-ngoni-kingdom|Mpezeni's Ngoni Kingdom]] in 1898 and bringing the [[s:bemba-kingdom|Bemba Kingdom]] under control in 1898-1899. An Order in Council of 1900 established North-Eastern [[s:rhodesia|Rhodesia]] under company administration.
north-eastern-rhodesia.r: The administrator [[e:robert-codrington|Robert Codrington]] governed from [[e:chipata|Fort Jameson]], now Chipata, with a small staff of officials. Hut tax pushed men to work in the mines of [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] and [[e:katanga|Katanga]] and on farms. Missionaries, especially the White Fathers among the [[s:bemba-kingdom|Bemba]], spread schooling, and the end of [[e:slave-raiding|slave raiding]] changed local politics.
north-eastern-rhodesia.e: In 1911 North-Eastern [[s:rhodesia|Rhodesia]] was merged with [[s:north-western-rhodesia|North-Western Rhodesia]] to form [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]], with its capital at [[e:livingstone-zambia|Livingstone]], and its territory later became the eastern and northern provinces of [[e:zambia|Zambia]].

nandgaon-state.t: A Chhattisgarh state ruled by Vaishnava Bairagi mahants, whose capital Rajnandgaon grew around a large cotton mill.
nandgaon-state.o: Nandgaon was a zamindari held by a line of Bairagi mahants, [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnava]] religious leaders, under the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]]. Around 1830 it emerged as a distinct holding, and the British recognised its chief as a feudatory ruler after taking over the [[e:nagpur|Nagpur]] territories.
nandgaon-state.r: Because the rulers were celibate ascetics, succession often passed from guru to disciple until the British accepted hereditary succession. The capital was renamed Rajnandgaon, and the [[e:bengal|Bengal]] [[e:nagpur|Nagpur]] [[e:cotton|Cotton]] Mills opened there in the 1890s. The state belonged to the [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]] feudatory states.
nandgaon-state.e: Nandgaon acceded to [[e:india|India]] and on 1 January 1948 was merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces and Berar]]; Rajnandgaon is now a district headquarters in [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].

northern-wei.t: The Tuoba Xianbei dynasty that reunified northern China in 439, carved the Yungang and Longmen grottoes and introduced the equal-field system.
northern-wei.o: [[e:emperor-daowu-of-northern-wei|Tuoba Gui]] restored the [[e:tuoba|Tuoba]] state of Dai in 386 and soon renamed it Wei. After defeating [[s:later-yan|Later Yan]] at [[e:battle-of-canhe-slope|Canhe Slope]] in 395, he took the [[e:north-china-plain|North China Plain]] and in 398 made [[e:datong|Pingcheng]] (Datong) his capital. [[e:emperor-taiwu-of-northern-wei|Emperor Taiwu]] completed the conquest of the north by taking [[s:northern-liang|Northern Liang]] in 439.
northern-wei.r: The Northern Wei ruled a mostly Chinese population through a [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] military aristocracy and Chinese officials. [[e:empress-dowager-feng|Empress Dowager Feng]] introduced the [[e:equal-field-system|equal-field]] system of land allotment in 485. [[e:emperor-xiaowen-of-northern-wei|Emperor Xiaowen]] moved the capital to [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]] in 494, banned [[e:xianbei|Xianbei]] dress and language at court and adopted the surname Yuan. Despite [[e:emperor-taiwu-of-northern-wei|Taiwu]]'s persecution of 446, [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] flourished, producing the [[e:yungang-grottoes|Yungang]] and [[e:longmen-grottoes|Longmen]] grottoes.
northern-wei.e: The Six Garrisons rebellion of 523 by neglected frontier troops shattered the state, and the general [[e:erzhu-rong|Erzhu Rong]] massacred the court in 528. In 534 to 535 the dynasty split into [[s:eastern-wei|Eastern Wei]] and [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]], controlled by [[e:gao-huan|Gao Huan]] and [[e:yuwen-tai|Yuwen Tai]].

nayar.t: The independent domain of the Cora people in the Sierra del Nayar, which held out against Spanish rule for nearly two centuries until 1722.
nayar.o: When [[e:nuno-de-guzman|Nuño de Guzmán]] conquered western [[s:mexico|Mexico]] in 1529-31, the [[e:cora-people|Cora]] (Náayeri) of the rugged [[e:sierra-del-nayar|Sierra del Nayar]] remained beyond Spanish control. Their mountain stronghold, centred on the [[e:mesa-del-nayar|Mesa del Nayar]], became a refuge for groups fleeing colonial rule, especially after the [[e:mixton-war|Mixtón War]] of 1540-42.
nayar.r: The [[e:cora-people|Cora]] were led by a ruler bearing the title Tonati, and their main temple on the [[e:mesa-del-nayar|Mesa del Nayar]] held the revered remains of an ancestral ruler, [[e:nayarit|Nayarit]], which gave the region its name. Their remote position allowed them to trade with Spanish towns, including in salt, while refusing missionaries and tribute.
nayar.e: After failed negotiations, a Spanish expedition under Juan Flores de San Pedro stormed the [[e:mesa-del-nayar|Mesa del Nayar]] in 1722, and the ancestor's remains were sent to [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]] and burnt. [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] missions followed. The modern state of [[e:nayarit|Nayarit]] takes its name from this domain, and the [[e:cora-people|Cora]] survive.

nuceria-alfaterna.t: Oscan city of southern Campania that led a league including Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae before becoming an ally of Rome.
nuceria-alfaterna.o: Nuceria Alfaterna, modern [[e:nocera-inferiore|Nocera Inferiore]], grew in the [[e:sarno-river|Sarno]] valley inland from the [[e:bay-of-naples|Bay of Naples]], on the route between [[e:campania|Campania]] and the [[e:gulf-of-salerno|Gulf of Salerno]]. Its population was [[e:oscan-language|Oscan]]-speaking by the 5th century BCE, and earlier settlement shows Etruscan and Greek contacts.
nuceria-alfaterna.r: Nuceria headed a league of towns in the [[e:sarno-river|Sarno]] valley and along the coast, including [[e:pompeii|Pompeii]], [[e:herculaneum|Herculaneum]], [[e:stabiae|Stabiae]] and [[e:sorrento|Surrentum]], and issued [[e:silver|silver]] coins in [[e:oscan-language|Oscan]] with the name of the Alfaterni. It controlled a fertile plain producing grain, wine and fruit. Little else is known of its institutions.
nuceria-alfaterna.e: During the [[e:second-samnite-war|Second Samnite War]] Nuceria fought [[e:rome|Rome]] but submitted in 308 BCE and became an ally on favourable terms. [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] destroyed it in 216 BCE for staying loyal to Rome, and it was later rebuilt. In 59 CE a riot between Nucerians and Pompeians in [[e:pompeii|Pompeii's]] amphitheatre was recorded by [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]].

nabhani-dynasty.t: A line of kings who ruled the Omani interior from Bahla for nearly five centuries between periods of Ibadi imamate.
nabhani-dynasty.o: The Banu Nabhan, an Arab tribe of the Azd, took power in inland [[e:oman|Oman]] in the mid-12th century, as the Ibadi [[e:imamate|imamate]] weakened. Ruling as maliks, or kings, from [[e:bahla|Bahla]] and its great fort, they governed the interior while the coast was dominated by [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Hormuz]].
nabhani-dynasty.r: Unlike elected Ibadi [[e:imam|imams]], the Nabhanis ruled by hereditary right, and Ibadi scholars often condemned them as tyrants. Their power waxed and waned; elected imams sometimes ruled alongside or instead of them from the 15th century. Their era is poorly documented, but the poet-king [[e:sulayman-ibn-sulayman-al-nabhani|Sulayman ibn Sulayman al-Nabhani]] is remembered, and [[e:bahla|Bahla's]] walls and fort date largely from this period.
nabhani-dynasty.e: From the 16th century the Portuguese took the coast, including [[s:portuguese-muscat|Portuguese Muscat]]. In 1624 Ibadi scholars elected [[e:nasir-ibn-murshid|Nasir ibn Murshid]] as [[e:imam|imam]], founding the [[s:yaaruba-dynasty|Ya'aruba dynasty]], which reunited [[e:oman|Oman]] and ended Nabhani rule.

nasrid-maliks-of-sistan.t: Descendants of the Saffarids who ruled Sistan as hereditary maliks under a succession of overlords for two centuries.
nasrid-maliks-of-sistan.o: After the [[s:ghaznavid-empire|Ghaznavid Empire]] absorbed [[e:sistan|Sistan]], a branch of the old [[s:saffarid-dynasty|Saffarid dynasty]] regained local power. In 1029 [[e:abul-fadl-nasr-ibn-ahmad|Abu'l-Fadl Nasr ibn Ahmad]] established himself at [[e:zaranj|Zaranj]], founding a line of maliks often called the Nasrids or Maliks of Nimruz.
nasrid-maliks-of-sistan.r: The maliks governed the irrigated delta of the [[e:helmand-river|Helmand]] as local hereditary rulers, accepting the overlordship in turn of the [[s:ghaznavid-empire|Ghaznavids]], the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]], the [[s:ghurid-sultanate|Ghurid Sultanate]] and the [[s:khwarazmian-empire|Khwarazmian Empire]]. The anonymous [[e:tarikh-i-sistan|Tarikh-i Sistan]], a Persian local history, reflects their court's pride in [[e:sistan|Sistan's]] past, from the hero [[e:rostam|Rustam]] to the [[s:saffarid-dynasty|Saffarids]]. [[e:taj-al-din-harb|Taj al-Din Harb]], who reigned for nearly fifty years until 1215, was the most notable of the line.
nasrid-maliks-of-sistan.e: The Mongol invasion devastated [[e:sistan|Sistan]] in the early 1220s, and the last Nasrid rulers were killed around 1225. Local rule soon passed to the [[s:mihrabanid-dynasty|Mihrabanid dynasty]].

naigawan-rebai-state.t: A tiny chiefship of the Bundelkhand Agency, recognised by the British in 1807.
naigawan-rebai-state.o: Naigawan Rebai was confirmed by a British sanad in 1807 as one of the small holdings left in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] after British supremacy replaced [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] influence.
naigawan-rebai-state.r: Little is recorded beyond its listing as a minor, non-salute state of a few villages.
naigawan-rebai-state.e: After independence Naigawan Rebai was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states and absorbed by 1950.

northern-territories-of-the-gold-coast.t: The British protectorate over the savanna lands north of Ashanti, which supplied labour to the colony's south and became the north of Ghana in 1957.
northern-territories-of-the-gold-coast.o: In the 1890s [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] raced [[e:france|France]] and [[e:germany|Germany]] for the lands north of the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]], signing treaties with rulers such as those of [[s:mamprugu|Mamprugu]], the [[s:kingdom-of-dagbon|Kingdom of Dagbon]], the [[s:kingdom-of-gonja|Kingdom of Gonja]] and [[s:wala-state|Wala State]]. The boundaries were fixed by agreements of 1898-1899, and the [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] was formally established in 1901, with its capital later at [[e:tamale|Tamale]].
northern-territories-of-the-gold-coast.r: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] ran the territory cheaply, through chiefs and a few officials. It was treated mainly as a reservoir of labour for the gold mines and cocoa farms of the south, and as a recruiting ground for the army. Mission activity and schooling were limited, so the north entered the late colonial period far behind the south in education and infrastructure.
northern-territories-of-the-gold-coast.e: On 6 March 1957 the Northern Territories became part of independent [[e:ghana|Ghana]] alongside the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]], the [[s:ashanti-colony|Ashanti Colony]] and [[s:british-togoland|British Togoland]]. The gap between north and south remains a theme of Ghanaian politics.

nieuwe-republiek.t: A Boer republic carved out of Zululand in 1884 as payment for helping Dinuzulu win the Zulu throne.
nieuwe-republiek.o: After the [[e:anglo-zulu-war|Anglo-Zulu War]] [[s:zulu-kingdom|Zululand]] fell into civil war. In 1884 [[e:boers|Boers]] led by [[e:lucas-meyer|Lucas Meyer]], among them the young [[e:louis-botha|Louis Botha]], backed [[e:dinuzulu-kacetshwayo|Dinuzulu]], son of [[e:cetshwayo|Cetshwayo]], against [[e:zibhebhu-kamaphitha|Zibhebhu]], and in return claimed a huge tract of [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]] land, where they proclaimed the Nieuwe Republiek with Lucas Meyer as president.
nieuwe-republiek.r: The republic set up a [[e:volksraad-dutch-east-indies|Volksraad]] and founded its capital at [[e:vryheid|Vryheid]]. Its original claim covered much of [[s:zulu-kingdom|Zululand]], but [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] forced a reduction in 1886, recognising a smaller territory in exchange for the rest being left to the [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]]. The [[e:burghers|burghers]] were [[e:cattle|cattle]] and sheep farmers.
nieuwe-republiek.e: The Nieuwe Republiek joined the [[s:south-african-republic|South African Republic]] in 1888 as the [[e:vryheid|Vryheid]] district. After the [[e:second-boer-war|Second Boer War]] the district was transferred to the [[s:natal-colony|Natal Colony]] in 1903, and [[e:lucas-meyer|Lucas Meyer]] and [[e:louis-botha|Louis Botha]] became leading [[e:boers|Boer]] generals.

nationalist-government.t: The Kuomintang government of the Republic of China, which reunified the country in 1928 and led its resistance to Japan.
nationalist-government.o: After [[e:sun-yat-sen|Sun Yat-sen's]] death the [[s:canton-military-government|Canton Military Government]] was reorganised in July 1925 as the National Government under the [[e:kuomintang|Kuomintang]]. Its armies, trained at [[e:whampoa-military-academy|Whampoa]], set out on the [[e:northern-expedition|Northern Expedition]] in 1926, and after [[e:chiang-kai-shek|Chiang Kai-shek]] broke with the Communists in 1927, he established the government at [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]], taking [[e:beijing|Beijing]] in 1928.
nationalist-government.r: In theory a period of one-party tutelage before constitutional rule, the '[[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] decade' brought new roads, railways, a national currency and modern schools, but regional warlords kept power and the government fought a long war against the Communists. [[e:japan|Japan]] seized [[e:manchuria|Manchuria]] in 1931. After full-scale war began in 1937 the government moved to [[e:chongqing|Chongqing]], which survived years of bombing; [[e:china|China]] became one of the Allied powers.
nationalist-government.e: After [[e:japan|Japan's]] surrender, civil war with the Communists resumed. A constitution took effect, and in May 1948 the National Government gave way to constitutional government with [[e:chiang-kai-shek|Chiang]] as president. Defeated on the mainland, the [[s:republic-of-china|Republic of China]] moved to [[e:taiwan|Taiwan]] in 1949.

nogai-horde.t: A nomadic confederation of the Volga-Ural steppe founded by the emir Edigu's descendants, the main horse-breeding power between Russia and Central Asia.
nogai-horde.o: The Nogai Horde grew from the [[e:manghud|Mangit tribe]] led by [[e:edigu|Edigu]], the emir who dominated the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] around 1400. His descendants built a separate power on the steppes between the [[e:volga|Volga]] and the [[e:ural-river|Ural River]] in the mid-15th century, with [[e:saraychik|Saraychik]] on the Ural as their seat.
nogai-horde.r: Its rulers held the title bey rather than khan, as they were not [[e:genghisid-principle|Genghisids]], and governed through a council of mirzas. The [[e:nogais|Nogais]] were pastoral nomads whose huge herds of horses were sold to [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Muscovy]] and [[e:central-asia|Central Asia]]. They were allies or rivals to the [[s:khanate-of-kazan|Khanate of Kazan]], the [[s:astrakhan-khanate|Astrakhan Khanate]] and the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]] in turn.
nogai-horde.e: Russian conquest of [[e:kazan|Kazan]] and Astrakhan in the 1550s split the horde; the [[s:lesser-nogai-horde|Lesser Nogai Horde]] moved west under Crimean protection. The rest came under Russian influence, and the arrival of the [[s:kalmyk-khanate|Kalmyk Khanate]] in the 1630s drove the [[e:nogais|Nogais]] from the [[e:volga|Volga]] steppe.

negeri-sembilan.t: Confederation of nine Minangkabau-settled territories in the Malay Peninsula, with an elected ruler and matrilineal customary law.
negeri-sembilan.o: [[e:minangkabau-people|Minangkabau]] migrants from [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]] settled the hills inland from [[e:malacca|Malacca]] from the 15th century onward, forming small territories (luak) under their own chiefs. In 1773 the chiefs invited [[e:raja-melewar|Raja Melewar]], a prince of the [[e:pagaruyung|Pagaruyung]] royal house, to become their overlord, and he was installed as the first Yang di-Pertuan Besar at [[e:seri-menanti|Seri Menanti]].
negeri-sembilan.r: The ruler was chosen by the four great territorial chiefs, the [[e:undang|Undang]], rather than succeeding automatically. Society followed [[e:adat|adat]] perpatih, a matrilineal custom in which land passed through women and clans chose their leaders. [[e:minangkabau-people|Minangkabau]] architecture with curved roofs, and [[e:tin|tin]] mining in [[e:sungai-ujong|Sungai Ujong]], marked the region.
negeri-sembilan.e: Rivalries over [[e:tin|tin]] brought British intervention in [[e:sungai-ujong|Sungai Ujong]] in 1874; the confederation was reconstituted under British protection in 1895 and joined the [[s:federated-malay-states|Federated Malay States]]. It is now a state of [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]], and its ruler [[e:tuanku-abdul-rahman|Tuanku Abdul Rahman]] became the first king of independent [[s:federation-of-malaya|Malaya]] in 1957.

natukhaj.t: A self-governing Circassian people of the Black Sea coast around Anapa and Novorossiysk, among the first to fall to Russia in the 19th century.
natukhaj.o: The Natukhaj were one of the western [[e:circassians|Adyghe]] groups of [[s:circassia|Circassia]], living in the coastal hills between the lower Kuban, [[e:anapa|Anapa]] and [[e:tsemes-bay|Tsemes Bay]]. They appear as a distinct community in Ottoman and Russian sources from the 17th and 18th centuries; earlier history is not recorded separately.
natukhaj.r: Like the [[s:shapsugs|Shapsugs]] and [[s:abadzekhs|Abadzekhs]], the Natukhaj overthrew the authority of their princes and nobles in the late 18th century and governed through assemblies of elders and free households. They farmed, kept livestock and traded at the Ottoman fortress of [[e:anapa|Anapa]], built in 1781, through which slaves, honey and hides passed to Ottoman ports.
natukhaj.e: [[e:russia|Russia]] took [[e:anapa|Anapa]] in 1828 and built coastal forts on Natukhaj land, including [[e:novorossiysk|Novorossiysk]] in 1838. After a long resistance, the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] completed its conquest in 1864, and nearly all Natukhaj were expelled to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]].

new-caledonia.t: A French Pacific territory annexed in 1853, rich in nickel and long divided over independence between Kanak and settler communities.
new-caledonia.o: [[e:james-cook|James Cook]] named the main island in 1774, and Catholic and Protestant missions followed in the 1840s. [[e:france|France]] annexed New [[s:new-caledonia-darien|Caledonia]] in 1853 under [[e:napoleon-iii|Napoleon III]], partly to establish a penal colony. [[e:noumea|Port-de-France]], founded in 1854, was renamed Nouméa in 1866.
new-caledonia.r: Between 1864 and 1897 [[e:france|France]] transported about 22,000 convicts, among them deported [[e:communards|Communards]] such as [[e:louise-michel|Louise Michel]]. Nickel was discovered in 1864 and mining became the core of the economy. The indigenous [[e:kanak-people|Kanak]] were confined to reserves under the [[e:indigenat|indigénat]] code, and they rose in major revolts in 1878, led by [[e:atai|Ataï]], and in 1917. The colony rallied to [[s:free-france|Free France]] in 1940 and was a major American base in the [[e:pacific-war|Pacific War]].
new-caledonia.e: It became an overseas territory in 1946 and the [[e:kanak-people|Kanak]] gained citizenship. Violent conflict in the 1980s ended with the [[e:matignon-accords-1988|Matignon Accords]] of 1988 and the [[e:noumea-accord|Nouméa Accord]] of 1998. Referendums in 2018, 2020 and 2021 rejected independence, and deadly unrest broke out in 2024 over voting rights.

neapolitan-republic-1647-1648.t: A short-lived republic born of Masaniello's revolt against Spanish taxes in Naples, which briefly invited a French duke as its leader.
neapolitan-republic-1647-1648.o: In July 1647 a new tax on fruit sparked a rising in [[e:naples|Naples]] led by the fisherman [[e:masaniello|Tommaso Aniello]], known as Masaniello. He was murdered within days, but the revolt spread, and in October 1647 the gunsmith [[e:gennaro-annese|Gennaro Annese]] proclaimed a republic independent of Spanish rule in the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]].
neapolitan-republic-1647-1648.r: The rebels held most of the city while Spanish forces kept the castles and the fleet bombarded the town. They invited [[e:henry-ii-duke-of-guise|Henry II, Duke of Guise]], a French claimant to the Angevin inheritance, who arrived in November and took the title Duke of the Republic. Quarrels between Guise, Annese and the nobles, and limited French support, weakened the regime, and the provinces were divided between rebels and barons.
neapolitan-republic-1647-1648.e: In April 1648, while Guise was outside the city, Spanish troops under [[e:john-of-austria-the-younger|Don John of Austria]] retook [[e:naples|Naples]] with the help of Annese. Guise was captured, and Spanish rule was restored.

north-caucasian-emirate.t: A short-lived Islamic state in Chechnya and Dagestan proclaimed by Sheikh Uzun-Haji in 1919 to fight Denikin's White army.
north-caucasian-emirate.o: After [[e:anton-denikin|Denikin]]'s [[e:volunteer-army|Volunteer Army]] overran the [[s:mountainous-republic-of-the-northern-caucasus|Mountainous Republic of the Northern Caucasus]] in 1919, the elderly Naqshbandi sheikh [[e:uzun-haji|Uzun-Haji]], who had long called for a revival of [[e:imam-shamil|Shamil]]'s [[e:imamate|imamate]], proclaimed the North Caucasian [[e:emirate|Emirate]] in September 1919 in the mountains of [[e:chechnya|Chechnya]], with its seat at [[e:vedeno|Vedeno]].
north-caucasian-emirate.r: [[e:uzun-haji|Uzun-Haji]] ruled as emir under [[e:sharia|sharia]], with a government of religious leaders and Ottoman officers, and with a nominal Ottoman sultan as protector. The [[e:emirate|emirate]] formed an army that waged [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] war against the [[e:white-movement|Whites]] in alliance of convenience with the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Bolsheviks]].
north-caucasian-emirate.e: With the defeat of the [[e:white-movement|Whites]], the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] entered the region in 1920. [[e:uzun-haji|Uzun-Haji]] died in March 1920, and the [[e:emirate|emirate]] was dissolved as the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]] established Soviet rule in the [[e:north-caucasus|North Caucasus]].

nan-kingdom.t: A northern Thai principality in the Nan valley that kept its own rulers for six centuries under Sukhothai, Lan Na, Burma and Siam.
nan-kingdom.o: Nan was founded by Tai chiefs in the upper Nan valley; chronicles give 1282 as a founding date at [[e:pua-district|Pua]], with the seat later moved to the present city of Nan in 1368. It was linked by kinship with [[e:phayao|Phayao]] and had early ties to [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]].
nan-kingdom.r: The rulers of Nan governed a mountainous territory of [[e:rice|rice]] valleys, salt [[e:well|wells]] at [[e:bo-kluea-district|Bo Kluea]] and forest trade. They were [[e:vassal|vassals]] in turn of [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]], [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]] from 1449, Burmese kings from 1558, and Siam from the late 18th century. Its temples, such as [[e:wat-phumin|Wat Phumin]] with its murals, reflect a distinct Tai Lue-influenced style.
nan-kingdom.e: Under the [[s:rattanakosin-kingdom|Rattanakosin Kingdom]] Nan kept its princes but lost autonomy through the provincial reforms of the 1890s. When the last ruler, [[e:chao-mahaphrom-surathada|Chao Mahaphrom Surathada]], died in 1931, the title was not filled and Nan became an ordinary province of [[s:thailand|Thailand]].

na-japan.t: An early Japanese polity near modern Fukuoka whose ruler received a gold seal from the Han emperor in 57 CE, one of the first datable events in Japanese history.
na-japan.o: Na grew up in the [[e:fukuoka|Fukuoka]] plain of northern [[e:kyushu|Kyushu]] during the Yayoi period, when wet [[e:rice|rice]] farming and metalworking spread from [[e:korea|Korea]]. Rich burials at [[e:sugu-okamoto|Sugu-Okamoto]], with bronze mirrors and weapons, point to a powerful local elite by the 1st century BCE.
na-japan.r: Known only from Chinese records and archaeology, Na was one of many small Wa polities. The [[e:book-of-the-later-han|Book of the Later Han]] records that its king sent envoys to [[e:emperor-guangwu-of-han|Emperor Guangwu]] in 57 and received a seal; a gold seal reading King of Na of Wa of Han was found on [[e:shikanoshima|Shikanoshima]] island in 1784.
na-japan.e: The 3rd-century Wei records list Na, with some 20,000 households, among the countries under Queen [[e:himiko|Himiko]] of [[s:yamatai|Yamatai]]. It was later absorbed into the [[s:yamato|Yamato]] realm.

ndebele-kingdom.t: Mzilikazi's militarised kingdom, which migrated from the highveld to western Zimbabwe and fell to the British South Africa Company in 1893.
ndebele-kingdom.o: [[e:mzilikazi|Mzilikazi]], a Khumalo commander under [[e:shaka-zulu-king|Shaka]], broke away around 1822 with a few hundred followers and moved onto the highveld, absorbing [[e:sotho-tswana-peoples|Sotho-Tswana]] communities as he went. Defeated by [[e:voortrekkers|Voortrekkers]] and [[e:griqua|Griqua]] at [[e:battle-of-mosega|Mosega]] and on the [[e:marico-river|Marico]] in 1837, the Ndebele crossed the [[e:limpopo|Limpopo]] and rebuilt the kingdom in what is now western [[e:zimbabwe|Zimbabwe]].
ndebele-kingdom.r: Society was organised in regimental towns, with a ranked order of Zansi of [[e:nguni|Nguni]] origin, Enhla from the highveld and Hole drawn from local [[e:shona|Shona]]. The king controlled [[e:cattle|cattle]] and raiding, and Shona chiefdoms paid tribute. [[e:lobengula|Lobengula]], who succeeded in 1870, built his capital at [[e:bulawayo|Bulawayo]] and tried to balance concession-seekers, but the 1888 [[e:rudd-concession|Rudd Concession]] opened the way to [[e:cecil-rhodes|Cecil Rhodes]].
ndebele-kingdom.e: The [[e:british-south-africa-company|British South Africa Company]] invaded in 1893, [[e:bulawayo|Bulawayo]] was burnt and [[e:lobengula|Lobengula]] died in early 1894. The 1896 rising was crushed, and the territory became Matabeleland within [[s:company-rule-in-rhodesia|Company rule in Rhodesia]].

nezak-huns.t: A dynasty of Hunnic origin that ruled Kapisa and Kabul from the late 5th century, known from coins bearing a crown topped by a buffalo head.
nezak-huns.o: The Nezak rulers emerged south of the [[e:hindu-kush|Hindu Kush]] around 484, probably as one of the Hunnic groups that followed the [[s:kidarite-kingdom|Kidarite Kingdom]] and [[s:alchon-huns|Alchon Huns]] into the region. Their coins, modelled on Sasanian issues, name the ruler as 'Nezak shah' in [[e:middle-persian|Pahlavi]] script.
nezak-huns.r: They ruled from [[e:kapisa|Kapisa]], near modern [[e:bagram|Bagram]], and the [[e:kabul|Kabul]] valley over a population that was largely Buddhist and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]]. The Chinese pilgrim [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]] visited Kapisa in 630 and described a prosperous kingdom with many monasteries and a [[e:kshatriya|Kshatriya]] king. Little is known about individual rulers beyond the coins.
nezak-huns.e: In the mid-7th century the Nezak faced Arab raids from [[e:sistan|Sistan]] and pressure from the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turks]]. Around 665 they were overthrown by the [[s:turk-shahis|Turk Shahis]], a Turkic dynasty that took over [[e:kabul|Kabul]] and [[e:kapisa|Kapisa]].

new-caledonia-darien.t: Scotland's disastrous attempt to found a trading colony on the Isthmus of Panama, whose failure helped push Scotland into union with England in 1707.
new-caledonia-darien.o: The Company of [[e:scotland|Scotland]], promoted by [[e:william-paterson-banker|William Paterson]] and backed by perhaps a fifth of Scotland's liquid capital, aimed to build an [[e:entrepot|entrepôt]] linking the Atlantic and Pacific. About 1,200 colonists sailed from [[e:leith|Leith]] in July 1698 and landed at Darien in November, founding Fort St Andrew and the town of New [[e:edinburgh|Edinburgh]].
new-caledonia-darien.r: The colony was run by a council of quarrelling members, with no clear leader. Settlers found the soil poor, the trade goods unsuited to local markets and the climate deadly; fever killed hundreds. [[e:william-iii-of-england|William III]], wary of offending [[e:spain|Spain]], forbade English colonies to supply them. Relations with the local [[e:guna-people|Guna people]] were friendly, but Spain regarded the colony as an intrusion.
new-caledonia-darien.e: The first settlers abandoned Darien in June 1699. A second expedition arrived later that year, won a skirmish at [[e:battle-of-toubacanti|Toubacanti]], but capitulated to a Spanish siege at the end of March 1700 and left in April. The loss of capital weakened Scottish resistance to union, and the 1707 [[e:acts-of-union-1707|Act of Union]] included compensation for the company's investors.

neo-elamite-kingdom.t: The last phase of Elam, a determined enemy of Assyria that was crushed by Ashurbanipal but passed its scribal culture on to the Persians.
neo-elamite-kingdom.o: After a dark period following the fall of the [[s:middle-elamite-kingdom|Middle Elamite kingdom]], [[e:elam|Elam]] reappears in the 8th century BCE as a kingdom centred on [[e:susa|Susa]] and the highlands of [[e:khuzestan|Khuzestan]] and [[e:fars|Fars]]. Its kings sought to resist the expanding [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], often by backing Babylonian rebels.
neo-elamite-kingdom.r: [[e:humban-nikash-i|Humban-nikash I]] fought [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] at Der in 720 BCE, and Elamite armies supported [[e:merodach-baladan-ii|Merodach-baladan]] of [[s:bit-yakin|Bit-Yakin]] and fought [[e:sennacherib|Sennacherib]] at [[e:battle-of-halule|Halule]] in 691 BCE. Internal rivalries, often exploited by [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]], produced frequent coups. Elamite religion centred on [[e:inshushinak|Inshushinak]] at [[e:susa|Susa]]. Assyrian reliefs at [[e:nineveh|Nineveh]] show the [[e:battle-of-ulai|Battle of Til-Tuba]] in 653 BCE, where King [[e:teumman|Teumman]] was beheaded.
neo-elamite-kingdom.e: [[e:ashurbanipal|Ashurbanipal]] sacked Susa around 646 BCE, desecrating royal tombs and temples. Smaller Neo-[[e:elamite-confederation|Elamite kingdoms]] survived until [[e:cyrus-the-great|Cyrus the Great]] absorbed them into the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] around 539 BCE. Elamite remained an administrative language of the [[e:persians|Persians]], as the [[e:persepolis|Persepolis]] tablets show.

new-sweden.t: Sweden's short-lived colony on the Delaware River, which introduced the log cabin to North America before falling to the Dutch in 1655.
new-sweden.o: The New [[e:sweden|Sweden]] Company, with [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and Swedish investors, sent the ships [[e:kalmar-nyckel|Kalmar Nyckel]] and Fogel Grip under [[e:peter-minuit|Peter Minuit]], former director of [[s:new-netherland|New Netherland]]. In 1638 they bought land from the [[e:lenape|Lenape]] and built [[e:fort-christina|Fort Christina]], at what is now [[e:wilmington-delaware|Wilmington, Delaware]], named after [[e:christina-queen-of-sweden|Queen Christina]].
new-sweden.r: The colony never had more than a few hundred settlers, many of them [[e:finns|Finns]] from the forests of [[e:sweden|Sweden]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-finland|Finland]], who brought the log cabin with them. Governor [[e:johan-bjornsson-printz|Johan Printz]], in office from 1643 to 1653, ruled from [[e:tinicum-island|Tinicum Island]], built forts along the river and traded [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and tobacco with the [[e:lenape|Lenape]] and [[s:susquehannock|Susquehannock]].
new-sweden.e: In 1654 Governor [[e:johan-risingh|Johan Risingh]] seized the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] [[e:fort-casimir|Fort Casimir]], provoking a response. In 1655 [[e:peter-stuyvesant|Peter Stuyvesant]] of [[s:new-netherland|New Netherland]] arrived with ships and soldiers, and New [[e:sweden|Sweden]] surrendered. The settlers stayed and kept their Lutheran churches, such as [[e:gloria-dei-old-swedes-church|Gloria Dei]] in [[e:philadelphia|Philadelphia]], under Dutch and later English rule.

north-hsenwi.t: The northern half of the partitioned Shan state of Hsenwi, on the China border, which kept its saopha under British and Burmese rule until 1959.
north-hsenwi.o: In 1888 the British divided the old Shan state of [[s:hsenwi-state|Hsenwi]], torn by civil war, into two parts. North Hsenwi, with its capital at Hsenwi town, covered the north-eastern lands along the frontier with [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]], including [[e:lashio|Lashio]] and the Kutkai area.
north-hsenwi.r: The saopha of North [[s:hsenwi-state|Hsenwi]] governed a large and ethnically mixed territory of Shan, [[e:kachin-people|Kachin]], [[e:palaung|Palaung]], Chinese and Wa peoples, with trade routes to [[e:china|China]]. The [[s:myanmar|Burma]] Road, opened in 1938 to supply Nationalist China, ran through it via [[e:lashio|Lashio]], and the region saw heavy fighting in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]]. It was part of the [[s:federated-shan-states|Federated Shan States]] from 1922.
north-hsenwi.e: North [[s:hsenwi-state|Hsenwi]] became part of [[e:shan-state|Shan State]] in independent [[s:myanmar|Burma]] in 1948, and its saopha surrendered his powers in 1959. The area later became a centre of ethnic insurgency and the border trade around [[e:muse-myanmar|Muse]].

nuevo-santander.t: Spanish frontier province on the Gulf of Mexico, colonised in a planned campaign by José de Escandón, that became the Mexican state of Tamaulipas and southern Texas.
nuevo-santander.o: The Gulf coast north of [[e:tampico|Tampico]] was held by independent peoples such as the [[e:coahuiltecan|Coahuiltecans]] and resisted Spanish settlement for two centuries. In 1746 the [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] commissioned [[e:jose-de-escandon|José de Escandón]] to colonise it, and from 1748 he founded over twenty towns and missions between the [[e:panuco-river|Pánuco]] and [[e:nueces-river|Nueces]] rivers, including Camargo, [[e:reynosa|Reynosa]] and, in 1755, [[e:laredo|Laredo]].
nuevo-santander.r: [[e:jose-de-escandon|Escandón]] governed as colonist and military commander, granting land to settler families from [[e:nuevo-leon|Nuevo León]] and Querétaro who raised [[e:cattle|cattle]], sheep and horses on large ranchos. The towns were small, defended by soldier-settlers, and missions tried to convert local hunter-gatherers, many of whom died or were displaced. The province formed part of [[s:new-spain|New Spain]] and at times came under the [[s:commandancy-general-of-the-internal-provinces|Commandancy General of the Internal Provinces]].
nuevo-santander.e: With Mexican independence in 1821 the province passed to [[s:mexico|Mexico]] and in 1824 became the state of [[e:tamaulipas|Tamaulipas]]. The lands north of the [[e:rio-grande|Rio Grande]], disputed after Texan independence, went to the [[s:united-states|United States]] in 1848; the ranching culture of the region shaped the later cowboy and vaquero tradition.

nanda-empire.t: The first empire of the Ganges valley, whose wealth and great army were feared even by Alexander's troops.
nanda-empire.o: Around 345 BCE [[e:mahapadma-nanda|Mahapadma Nanda]], said by tradition to be of low birth, overthrew the last [[e:shishunaga-dynasty|Shishunaga]] ruler of the [[s:kingdom-of-magadha|Kingdom of Magadha]]. The [[e:puranas|Puranas]] call him a destroyer of the old [[e:kshatriya|Kshatriya]] dynasties, and he extended Magadhan rule over the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges plain]] and probably into [[s:kingdom-of-kalinga|Kalinga]], ruling from [[e:pataliputra|Pataliputra]].
nanda-empire.r: The Nandas built a centralised state with a large standing army; Greek writers reported 200,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, thousands of [[e:chariot|chariots]] and [[e:war-elephant|war elephants]]. They were famous for their treasury, filled by heavy taxes, and for public works such as canals. Their fearsome reputation helped convince Alexander's soldiers to refuse to march beyond the [[e:beas|Beas]] in 326 BCE. [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] and Buddhist sources alike remember the last king, [[e:dhana-nanda|Dhana Nanda]], as greedy and unpopular.
nanda-empire.e: Around 322 BCE [[e:chandragupta-maurya|Chandragupta Maurya]], guided according to tradition by the [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] [[e:chanakya|Chanakya]], overthrew [[e:dhana-nanda|Dhana Nanda]] and founded the [[s:maurya-empire|Maurya Empire]], which inherited the Nanda administration and capital.

natal-colony.t: Britain's sugar colony on the Indian Ocean coast of South Africa, whose Indian labourers and segregation policies shaped later South Africa.
natal-colony.o: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed the [[s:natalia-republic|Natalia Republic]] in 1843 to keep the [[e:boers|Boers]] from a port of their own. Natal was first run as a district of the [[s:cape-colony|Cape Colony]] and became a separate colony in 1856, governed from [[e:pietermaritzburg|Pietermaritzburg]] with [[e:durban|Durban]] as its port.
natal-colony.r: [[e:theophilus-shepstone|Theophilus Shepstone]], Secretary for Native Affairs, set up reserves ruled by chiefs under customary law, a model for later segregation. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar plantations]] on the coast relied on indentured labourers from [[e:india|India]] from 1860; [[e:mahatma-gandhi|Gandhi]] began his political career in Natal's Indian community. Responsible government came in 1893, and [[s:zulu-kingdom|Zululand]] was incorporated in 1897. The [[e:bambatha-rebellion|Bambatha rebellion]] against a poll tax was crushed in 1906.
natal-colony.e: Natal's English-speaking voters were wary of [[e:afrikaners|Afrikaner]] dominance, but in 1910 the colony joined the [[s:union-of-south-africa|Union of South Africa]] as [[e:natal-province|Natal Province]]. Merged with the [[s:zulu-kingdom|KwaZulu]] [[e:bantustan|homeland]] in 1994, it is now the province of [[e:kwazulu-natal|KwaZulu-Natal]].

new-haven-colony.t: A strict Puritan colony on Long Island Sound, governed by Bible-based law, which was merged into Connecticut after 1664.
new-haven-colony.o: In 1638 the [[e:london|London]] minister [[e:john-davenport|John Davenport]] and the merchant [[e:theophilus-eaton|Theophilus Eaton]] led a wealthy company of [[e:puritans|Puritans]] to Quinnipiac on [[e:long-island-sound|Long Island Sound]], buying land from the local people. They laid out New Haven on a grid of nine squares, and settlements at [[e:milford-connecticut|Milford]], [[e:guilford-connecticut|Guilford]], [[e:stamford-connecticut|Stamford]], [[e:branford-connecticut|Branford]] and [[e:southold-new-york|Southold]] on Long Island later joined them.
new-haven-colony.r: Only church members could vote or hold office, and the colony based its laws closely on scripture, doing without [[e:jury-trial|trial by jury]]. [[e:theophilus-eaton|Eaton]] served as governor until his death in 1658. The founders hoped for a great trading port, but their richly laden ship sent to [[e:england|England]] in 1646 vanished at sea. In 1661 the colony sheltered the regicides [[e:edward-whalley|Edward Whalley]] and [[e:william-goffe|William Goffe]] from royal agents.
new-haven-colony.e: Without a royal charter, New Haven was included in [[e:connecticut|Connecticut's]] charter of 1662 and, after resistance, accepted union with the [[s:connecticut-colony|Connecticut Colony]] in 1664 to 1665. New Haven remained a co-capital of Connecticut until 1875.

nagod-state.t: A Parihar Rajput state in Baghelkhand, ruled first from Unchahara and later from Nagod, among the states of central India's Bagelkhand Agency.
nagod-state.o: The [[e:parihar|Parihar]] rulers claimed descent from the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty]] and tradition dates their rule in the area to 1344, with an early seat at Unchahara. The capital moved to [[e:nagod|Nagod]] in the 18th century.
nagod-state.r: [[e:nagod|Nagod]] was a small agricultural state between Rewa and [[s:panna-state|Panna]]. It came under British protection in the early 19th century and was later administered through the [[e:baghelkhand-agency|Bagelkhand Agency]]. Little detailed history is recorded.
nagod-state.e: After independence [[e:nagod|Nagod]] joined [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]], which merged into [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956. It is now in [[e:satna-district|Satna district]].

namnetes.t: Gallic people of the Loire estuary, allies of the Veneti against Caesar, who gave their name to the city of Nantes.
namnetes.o: The Namnetes lived on the north bank of the lower [[e:loire|Loire]], with a port called [[e:nantes|Condevicnum]] or Portus Namnetum on the site of Nantes. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] and Ptolemy place them between the [[s:veneti|Veneti]] and the [[s:pictones|Pictones]], and Greek writers knew the Loire mouth as a trading point for Atlantic [[e:tin|tin]], linked to the earlier port of [[e:corbilo|Corbilo]].
namnetes.r: Little is known of their government. They took part in the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic trade]] of the Armorican peoples and struck gold and [[e:silver|silver]] coins of Armorican style.
namnetes.e: In 56 BCE the Namnetes sent help to the [[s:veneti|Veneti]] in their naval war against [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]] and shared in their defeat. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their port grew into the town of [[e:nantes|Condevicnum]], renamed after the people as Namnetes, the origin of the name Nantes.

nakhon-si-thammarat-kingdom.t: The major southern Thai kingdom of the Malay Peninsula, heir to Tambralinga, which spread Sinhalese Buddhism to Sukhothai and was a key vassal of Ayutthaya.
nakhon-si-thammarat-kingdom.o: The [[e:nakhon-si-thammarat|Nakhon Si Thammarat]] Kingdom grew out of [[s:tambralinga|Tambralinga]] in the late 13th century, as the city of Nakhon Si Thammarat, called Ligor by Europeans, became a Thai-ruled Buddhist centre. [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]] inscriptions mention monks invited from Nakhon Si Thammarat to bring [[e:theravada-buddhism|Sinhalese Theravada Buddhism]] north.
nakhon-si-thammarat-kingdom.r: The kingdom ruled the southern peninsula and claimed tribute from Malay states, a role sometimes described in legend as the twelve naksat cities. The great stupa of [[e:wat-phra-mahathat-woramahawihan|Wat Phra Mahathat]], rebuilt in Sinhalese style, made it a pilgrimage centre. From the 14th century it was a senior [[e:vassal|vassal]] and then a first-class province of [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]], ruled by appointed governors.
nakhon-si-thammarat-kingdom.e: When [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] fell in 1767, the governor [[e:chao-nakhon-nu|Chao Nakhon Nu]] declared himself independent. [[e:taksin|Taksin]] of the [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi Kingdom]] captured [[e:nakhon-si-thammarat|Nakhon Si Thammarat]] in 1769 and restored it to Siamese rule. It remains an important provincial city of southern [[s:thailand|Thailand]].

nung-autonomous-territory.t: A French-backed autonomous zone of the Nung people in north-eastern Vietnam during the First Indochina War, led by Voong A Sang.
nung-autonomous-territory.o: In 1947 French authorities, seeking allies against the [[e:viet-minh|Viet Minh]], recognised an autonomous territory in the Hai Ninh area around [[e:mong-cai|Mong Cai]] for the [[e:nung-people|Nung]], as the largely Chinese-speaking border communities there were known. The local leader Voong A Sang, who had built up a militia, became its head.
nung-autonomous-territory.r: The territory was administered under French supervision with its own [[e:nung-people|Nung]] armed units, which fought alongside French forces. It was one of several ethnic autonomous areas, including the [[s:tai-federation|Tai Federation]], created as part of [[e:france|France's]] strategy of dividing Vietnamese nationalism. After 1950 it was formally placed under [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai's]] [[s:state-of-vietnam|State of Vietnam]].
nung-autonomous-territory.e: The [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] Accords of 1954 placed the area in [[s:democratic-republic-of-vietnam|North Vietnam]]. Voong A Sang and thousands of [[e:nung-people|Nung]] moved south, where Nung units served in the Army of the [[s:republic-of-vietnam|Republic of Vietnam]].
