new-spain.t: Spain's richest viceroyalty, centred on Mexico City, which for three centuries governed Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and the Philippines.
new-spain.o: After [[e:hernan-cortes|Hernán Cortés]] and his indigenous allies conquered the [[s:aztec-empire|Aztec Empire]] in 1521, [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]] was built on the ruins of [[e:tenochtitlan|Tenochtitlan]]. The Crown established an audiencia in 1527 and the viceroyalty in 1535, with [[e:antonio-de-mendoza|Antonio de Mendoza]] as the first [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]].
new-spain.r: [[e:viceroyalty-of-new-spain|New Spain]] oversaw the [[s:captaincy-general-of-guatemala|Captaincy General of Guatemala]], the [[s:captaincy-general-of-cuba|Captaincy General of Cuba]], the [[s:captaincy-general-of-the-philippines|Captaincy General of the Philippines]] and northern provinces such as [[s:spanish-texas|Spanish Texas]]. [[e:silver|Silver]] from [[e:zacatecas|Zacatecas]] and [[e:guanajuato|Guanajuato]] flowed to [[e:europe|Europe]] and, via the [[e:manila-galleon|Manila galleons]], to [[e:china|China]]. Indigenous communities paid tribute, and a society of Spaniards, Indigenous people, Africans and mixed castas developed. The Church, [[e:franciscans|Franciscans]] and the [[e:portuguese-inquisition|Inquisition]] shaped culture.
new-spain.e: [[e:miguel-hidalgo-y-costilla|Miguel Hidalgo's]] revolt of 1810 began a long war of independence. In 1821 [[e:agustin-de-iturbide|Agustín de Iturbide's]] [[e:plan-of-iguala|Plan of Iguala]] and the [[e:treaty-of-cordoba|Treaty of Córdoba]] ended Spanish rule, and [[e:viceroyalty-of-new-spain|New Spain]] was succeeded by the [[s:first-mexican-empire|First Mexican Empire]].
ru: Juan Vicente de Güemes, 2nd Count of Revillagigedo

northern-march.t: A Saxon frontier march east of the Elbe, lost to the Slavs in 983 and revived as the territory that became the March of Brandenburg.
northern-march.o: When [[e:gero-the-great|Margrave Gero]] died in 965 his huge march was split, and the northern part, between the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and the [[e:oder-river|Oder]] north of the [[e:havel|Havel]], became the Northern March. Its first margrave was [[e:dietrich-of-haldensleben|Dietrich of Haldensleben]], who ruled over the [[s:principality-of-the-hevelli|Hevelli]] and Lutician [[e:slavs|Slavs]].
northern-march.r: The Northern March was a military frontier, defended by castles and supported by the bishoprics of [[e:havelberg|Havelberg]] and [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]]. [[e:dietrich-of-haldensleben|Dietrich]]'s harsh rule helped provoke the [[e:great-slav-rising|Great Slav Rising]] of 983, after which German power collapsed east of the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and the margraves held only the [[e:altmark|Altmark]] on the west bank, around [[e:salzwedel|Salzwedel]] and [[e:stendal|Stendal]].
northern-march.e: In 1134 [[e:lothair-i|Lothair]] III granted the Northern March to the Ascanian [[e:albert-the-bear|Albert the Bear]]. After he secured [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] in 1157, he took the title of [[e:margrave-of-brandenburg|Margrave of Brandenburg]]. The old march, with the [[e:altmark|Altmark]] as its western core, became part of the [[s:margraviate-of-brandenburg|Margraviate of Brandenburg]].

nyasaland.t: The British protectorate around Lake Malawi that resisted federation with the Rhodesias and became independent Malawi.
nyasaland.o: In 1907 the [[s:british-central-africa-protectorate|British Central Africa Protectorate]], created by [[e:harry-johnston|Harry Johnston]] in 1891 after wars against Yao slave traders, was renamed the Nyasaland [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]]. It was given a governor, an executive council and a legislative council, with [[e:zomba|Zomba]] remaining the capital.
nyasaland.r: Nyasaland was a poor territory whose main export was labour: tens of thousands of men worked in the mines and farms of [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] and [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]], while planters in the [[e:shire-highlands|Shire Highlands]] grew tobacco and [[e:tea|tea]] using thangata [[e:tenancy|tenancy]]. In 1915 the [[e:baptists|Baptist]] preacher [[e:john-chilembwe|John Chilembwe]] led a short rising against planter abuses. Scottish missions made literacy unusually widespread, and the [[e:nyasaland-african-congress|Nyasaland African Congress]] was founded in 1944.
nyasaland.e: Nyasaland was joined to the [[s:federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland|Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland]] in 1953 against strong African opposition. [[e:hastings-banda|Hastings Kamuzu Banda]] returned in 1958, a state of emergency followed in 1959, and his [[e:malawi-congress-party|Malawi Congress Party]] won the 1961 elections. Nyasaland became independent as [[e:malawi|Malawi]] on 6 July 1964.

nawanagar-state.t: The Jadeja Rajput state of Saurashtra ruled by the Jams of Jamnagar, home of the cricketer Ranjitsinhji and a wartime refuge for Polish children.
nawanagar-state.o: In 1540 [[e:jam-rawal|Jam Rawal]], a [[e:jadeja|Jadeja Rajput]] from [[s:cutch-state|Kutch]], conquered the Halar region of [[e:kathiawar|Saurashtra]] and founded Nawanagar, the 'new town', later called Jamnagar after the dynasty's title.
nawanagar-state.r: Nawanagar was known for its pearl fisheries, textiles and port. In 1591 its forces fought the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] at [[e:battle-of-bhuchar-mori|Bhuchar Mori]], after which the Jams accepted imperial rule. [[e:ranjitsinhji|Jam Ranjitsinhji]] (r. 1907–1933), the famous cricketer, modernised Jamnagar. His nephew [[e:digvijaysinhji|Digvijaysinhji]] sheltered hundreds of Polish refugee children at [[e:balachadi|Balachadi]] during the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]].
nawanagar-state.e: In 1948 [[e:digvijaysinhji|Digvijaysinhji]] became [[e:rajpramukh|Rajpramukh]] of the new [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]], into which Nawanagar merged. Jamnagar is now a city in [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]].

naiman-khanate.t: The most westerly and literate of the Mongolian steppe powers before Genghis Khan, whose Uyghur scribes gave the Mongols their script.
naiman-khanate.o: The Naimans were a large tribal people in western [[s:mongolia|Mongolia]], between the [[e:altai-mountains|Altai]] mountains and the upper [[e:irtysh|Irtysh]], of Turkic or mixed Turkic and Mongolic origin; their name means 'the Eight' in Mongolian. By the 12th century they formed a khanate under a ruling family that bore Turkic titles.
naiman-khanate.r: The Naimans were pastoral nomads in close contact with the [[e:uyghurs|Uyghurs]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-qocho|Kingdom of Qocho]] and the [[s:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]]. Their court used Uyghur script and seals, and [[e:christianity|Christianity]] of the [[e:church-of-the-east|Church of the East]] and [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] had followers among them. After the death of [[e:inanch-bilge-khan|Inanch Bilge Khan]] in the 1190s the khanate split between his sons [[e:tayang-khan|Tayang Khan]] and [[e:buyruk-khan|Buyruk Khan]].
naiman-khanate.e: In 1204 [[e:genghis-khan|Temüjin]] defeated [[e:tayang-khan|Tayang Khan]] at [[e:battle-of-chakirmaut|Chakirmaut]], where Tayang died; [[e:buyruk-khan|Buyruk]] was killed in 1206. Tayang's son Küchlüg fled to the [[s:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]] and seized its throne. The captured [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] scribe [[e:tata-tonga|Tata-tonga]] taught the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] to write their language in Uyghur letters.
naiman-khanate.re: Tengrism, Church of the East, Buddhism

nongkhlaw-state.t: The Khasi state whose Syiem, U Tirot Sing, led the Anglo-Khasi War of 1829–1833 against British road-building through his lands.
nongkhlaw-state.o: Hima Nongkhlaw was one of the Khasi chiefdoms of the [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]] plateau, lying on the northern slopes towards the [[e:brahmaputra|Brahmaputra]] valley. Its origins are known from oral tradition, and the register's start date is approximate.
nongkhlaw-state.r: Nongkhlaw was ruled by a [[e:syiem|Syiem]] from a royal clan, chosen with clan elders, with succession through the female line. In the 1820s Syiem [[e:tirot-sing|U Tirot Sing]] agreed to let the British build a road from [[e:assam|Assam]] to [[e:sylhet|Sylhet]] through his territory. When the British began treating the hills as their own, his men attacked the post at Nongkhlaw in 1829, killing two British officers.
nongkhlaw-state.e: [[e:tirot-sing|U Tirot Sing]] waged [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] war until he surrendered in 1833; he died a prisoner in [[e:dhaka|Dhaka]] in 1835 and is honoured as a hero in [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]]. Nongkhlaw acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1948 and is now part of Meghalaya.
